entries.name: 3D Pinball for Windows: Space Cadet (SpaceCadetPinball)
entries.summary: Space Cadet on modern desktop systems using your own Windows or Full Tilt game resources. The official Windows player is a ZIP; upstream or you provide updates.

setup.title: Keep the player and your game resources together
setup.instruction: For the modern Windows x64 player, extract the complete SpaceCadetPinballx64Win.zip into a separate folder you control. Keep SpaceCadetPinball.exe, SDL2.dll and SDL2_mixer.dll together. Add your own original Windows Space Cadet or supported Full Tilt resources to that folder; the port download does not include them. The x86 and Windows XP packages are different alternatives. There is no installer or converter to finish.

setup.title: Save the player, then choose Play
setup.instruction: Select SpaceCadetPinball.exe with that folder as its working directory, save launch details, then choose Play separately. If the game reports missing resources, follow its folder search message and the upstream guide. macOS application packages and Linux distribution/Flatpak or source-build routes keep their own upstream installation instructions; a Windows ZIP does not establish their native qualification.

setup.title: Keep the intended table and its scores together
setup.instruction: For Release 2.1.0, use a separate working folder for the table data you intend to play. The player searches the working folder before its executable folder and user profile; it normally tries Full Tilt CADET.DAT before Windows PINBALL.DAT, then DEMO.DAT. Its Prefer 3D Pinball data option changes that file preference. Keep the matching resource set together rather than mixing editions. The same imgui_pb.ini stores options, controls and high-score names/scores; preserve it as a complete file with its verification value, not selected score lines. Other player copies can share that profile. Changing the runtime folder does not isolate it, and original Windows registry scores are not automatically imported.

setup_notes.title: Keep your profile and resources when updating
setup_notes.instruction: You or upstream provide updates to this external copy. Close the game and preserve your original/custom resources, any chosen external font, and the SpaceCadetPinball user profile before changing versions. On Windows the normal profile is %APPDATA%\SpaceCadetPinball and includes imgui_pb.ini; it is separate from the downloaded player folder. Verify your options and progress in the new copy before retiring the old one. Removing the Portcove registration leaves every external file untouched; it does not provide managed Update, Backup or Rollback.

limitations: Close the game and preserve your original/custom resources, any chosen external font, and the SpaceCadetPinball user profile before changing versions.

entries.name: 40 Winks / Faderz48
entries.summary: Build and play 40 Winks on Windows or Linux with upstream’s setup tools and your own clean USA Nintendo 64 ROM.

setup.title: Get the upstream setup for your platform
setup.instruction: Open the v0.1.7-alpha release linked below and pick the Windows x64 setup EXE or Linux x86-64 AppImage. Check the file against its SHA-256 sidecar before opening it. Both paths need a clean big-endian USA .z64 from your own game. Setup checks SHA-256 057232ef7618e25f5645df50d3cd45f08cb5a2cccb3e2fdf48faa8755c4ddb1a. Keep that original available for later launches.

setup.title: Build the playable copy once
setup.instruction: On Windows, open the upstream setup, select the matching ROM and choose a folder for the generated player. On Linux, install the development dependencies from the build guide, then open the upstream self-building AppImage, select the ROM and choose where to save the playable AppImage. First setup needs Internet access and builds locally. On later Windows launches open 40-Winks-PC-Port.exe from the output folder. On Linux reopen the original AppImage to start the locally built player.

setup_notes.title: Keep Windows settings and Controller Pak saves
setup_notes.instruction: Preserve %LOCALAPPDATA%\40-winks-pc-port when changing the player. The separate %LOCALAPPDATA%\40WinksBuild stores build tools and generated files.

setup_notes.title: Linux build requirements and launcher paths
setup_notes.instruction: Follow the tagged build guide for Git, Python, CMake, a C++20 compiler, SDL2 development files, Vulkan and the runtime dependencies. The builder tracks the selected ROM and playable AppImage under the 40-winks-pc-port directory in XDG_CONFIG_HOME. The first-run launcher suggests ~/Applications/40-Winks-Recompiled-x86_64.AppImage for the playable copy. Its build cache is under XDG_CACHE_HOME. Preserve the game data under XDG_DATA_HOME/40-winks-pc-port (normally ~/.local/share/40-winks-pc-port), or the data directory you explicitly chose.

limitations: The Windows setup is unsigned. Follow your usual executable trust settings.
Keep the original outside the build and player folders. Replacement builds and player data are managed through upstream.

setup.title: Prepare your own matching disc with the project’s tools
setup.instruction: Use an independently permitted complete The Sims original-Xbox Windows player, separate from any desktop, handheld or other console edition. Supply your own USA disc ISO/xiso or complete extracted game tree with default.xbe and all matching assets/movies. This title’s documented default.xbe is 2,183,168 bytes, SHA-1 40ab6f97e8ee3bf4102a5a7820dcb8047fc30097, title ID 0x4541002F; another revision is not interchangeable. The runtime compares the loaded XBE with its own compiled expected hash; a matching executable does not authenticate every disc byte. setup.title: Select the completed game player
setup.instruction: Select Sims1.exe, with its complete creating player directory as working directory and no arguments for normal launch. Keep its matching runtime DLLs, resources, notices and assets/ together. The Windows route uses Direct3D 12 and XAudio2; keep the supported host graphics/runtime dependencies installed upstream. The source locates assets/ beside the executable or in ancestor folders; preserve the actual selected tree rather than redirecting originals during attachment. Do not select build scripts, generators or another title’s executable.

setup.title: Close every game process before maintenance
setup.instruction: The Windows player runs the game in its own process, but an Xbox title reboot can start a separate executable. Portcove does not track that successor as part of this registration; this guide does not establish when this title uses it. Close the actual game and all companions before changing files or adding another copy. Registration status alone does not show that every process has stopped.

setup.title: Review launch details, then choose Play
setup.instruction: Review and consent to the selected executable, working folder and launch arguments, then choose Play separately. You and the project manage setup, version changes, recovery and all external files. Removing the registration leaves those files in place. Before changing versions, close every game process and keep the complete working player and all its data. Review and select the executable again if its files change. setup.instruction: Complete the supported upstream build from your own Ace Combat 5: The Unsung War USA SLUS-20851 original. setup.title: Select the completed game player
setup.instruction: Select the completed build/gcc/ac5.exe, with its creating project root as working directory. Use --data followed by the absolute generated directory containing ps2_image.bin, --disc followed by your absolute own ISO or extracted-disc directory, and --watchdog 0. That is the documented normal play command: the upstream watchdog otherwise abandons a no-field interval during the normal initial black screen. Do not select gsreplay, a compiler or a generator. Keep the adjacent shaders, SDL3.dll and libwinpthread-1.dll, with the driver Vulkan loader available.

setup.title: Allow the game to finish normally
setup.instruction: The normal player stays open for the game session until exit; --vblanks 0 is the documented default. A short diagnostic loop in the source does not establish a gameplay time limit. Portcove has not observed startup or gameplay for this route.

setup.title: Prepare the PS4 remake with upstream first
setup.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. The reviewed 0.70 Windows route is the Bluepoint2018 PS4 remake: CUSA08809 EU1.01 or CUSA08034 US1.00, with your own decrypted game folder containing eboot.bin, sce_module and sce_sys. PS2/PS3 releases are different inputs. Sound additionally needs your own console-dumped decrypted libSceNgs2.sprx and libSceUlt.sprx; those Sony modules are not supplied by this guide or covered by the runtime license. Follow upstream setup outside Portcove, select the correct game/modules and save settings before attachment.

setup.title: Keep the complete Windows package together
setup.instruction: The inspected0.70 SotC-PC.zip contains SotC-PC/SotC.exe, bin/bb-probe.exe, companion DLLs, _internal, scripts and launcher resources. Keep the entire extracted SotC-PC directory together in a writable location. SotC.exe is the frozen native frontend; selecting an internal probe, Python executable, DLL or original eboot.bin bypasses its saved setup. This registration does not download, extract or run setup.

setup.title: Select saved-settings play explicitly
setup.instruction: Select the prepared package’s SotC.exe, set its complete SotC-PC directory as working directory, and use the single argument --play. Review the exact selected intent, then request Play separately. With a valid saved game folder, this route waits for its --run child, which in turn waits for bin/bb-probe.exe. If setup is missing it opens the GUI instead: finish setup and close that attempt before retrying. No native run or child-cleanup observation is claimed by source inspection.

setup.title: Preserve all actual data locations
setup.instruction: The current package keeps launcher_settings.json in its user directory; the ordinary save/cache/log root is also user beside SotC.exe unless the saved user_dir or existing SOTC_USER_DIR selects another location. Keep the complete effective tree, sotc.ini, any legacy %APPDATA%/sotc-launcher/settings.json, original game/update/DLC folders and your console modules. The source can discover neighbouring -UPDATE/-patch folders and established source/data overrides. This guide sets no new override, moves no saves and promises no cross-copy or cross-version compatibility.

setup.title: Leave maintenance and shutdown with their owners
setup.instruction: Complete upstream updates, setup changes and repair outside an attached game session; the GUI updater can start an applier/successor. Close the actual game and all helpers before replacing files, retain independent recovery copies, then review/relink changed executable bytes. Let ordinary play end through the game before closing the tracked player. Forced termination is not proof of save flush or child quiescence. Portcove does not adopt updater successors or own runtime replacement.

setup.title: Check this release’s limits and required notices
setup.instruction: Preserve the project GPL notice and all component/NVIDIA notices; runtime licensing grants no rights to the original game or console firmware. Upstream performance, ending and GPU reports are attributable upstream claims. Maximum-texture crashes, some AMD GCN graphics problems and experimental frame generation/60FPS limitations remain in the selected upstream instructions. No Portcove gameplay, save/reload, installed-app or Supported acceptance is claimed. Removing registration preserves every external file; managed installation, update, rollback, backup and deletion are not offered.

limitations: Use only the independently permitted PS4-remake installation and console modules; retain all external player data and complete maintenance upstream.

entries.name: MediEvil / Alexbeav PSXRecomp
entries.summary: Build a native MediEvil player from your matching original PlayStation disc and BIOS.

setup.title: Use your original disc and BIOS
setup.instruction: Use your own MediEvil (USA) disc (SCUS-94227) with both its data and audio tracks, and your own retail SCPH-1001 BIOS. Keep the original files separately.

setup.title: Build the managed Windows or Linux player
setup.instruction: In Portcove, select the complete matching CHD and BIOS. Keep both files in place. Choose Play after Portcove builds the game.

setup.title: Prepare a separate Mac copy
setup.instruction: Extract the official ZIP for your Mac into a writable folder. Check the release notes for its macOS minimum, Python version and Homebrew dependencies. The v0.1.5 setup host requires openssl@3, sdl3, freetype and harfbuzz. Make the Xcode Command Line Tools, CMake, Ninja and Python 3 available, then choose Generate & rebuild in the upstream setup host with your matching CUE, both BIN files and retail BIOS.

setup.title: Add the completed Mac player
setup.instruction: In Portcove, select build-release/MediEvil_Recompiled and use build-release as the start folder. Keep the complete working kit and its companion files. You manage replacement and backups for this copy.

setup_notes.title: Keep your saves and diagnostics
setup_notes.instruction: Close the game before backing up. Portcove retains the declared files of its managed Windows and Linux players. For a Mac copy, preserve the complete working folder, including saves, settings, installed mods and any diagnostic location named beside the player.

limitations: Portcove checks the first data track and track count. Keep the complete disc intact.

The v0.1.4 playtest build records offline diagnostics by default, including starting memory cards, settings and inputs. Turn off Input Recording in that build to stop new recordings. The v0.1.5 standard kit omits the title's playtest diagnostics package. Review any capture or replay before sharing.

entries.name: Pro Pinball: Timeshock! / Alexbeav PSXRecomp
entries.summary: PlayStation port prepared with your own matching disc and any required BIOS. Complete setup with the project’s launcher; you manage this copy, its updates and your saved data.

setup.title: Download and unpack the setup kit
setup.instruction: Extract the complete official ZIP for your system into a separate writable folder. On Linux, follow the kit’s requirements for CMake, Ninja, Python 3 and a C/C++ compiler. Use Linux tools for the Linux build.

setup.title: Supply the matching original files
setup.instruction: Follow the upstream guide for the version you downloaded. entries.name: Amped 2 (Amped2-Recomp)
entries.summary: An experimental Linux x86-64 Amped 2 port. The Windows preview is explicitly unplayable and very slow, with only Wine/Proton testing. Use your own PAL/Europe original-Xbox disc: title 4D530041, XDK 5558, default.xbe SHA-1 38e63cd016bf084d999e0a911933a52191bfc378. The project supports a full Redump ISO, game-partition XISO or extracted folder. Keep every disc file in game_files/, with default.xbe directly at its root; other versions are untested. Portcove has not confirmed setup or gameplay.

setup.title: Play the experimental Linux release
setup.instruction: Use glibc 2.39 or later, SDL2 and a Vulkan driver. Extract the Linux tarball. Put your complete supported PAL Xbox disc files under game_files/ with default.xbe directly in that folder. Run ./run.sh from the extracted package. Run ./run.sh --settings to open graphics settings. setup.title: Use this original game and edition
setup.instruction: Use a complete installed original Baldur’s Gate II: Shadows of Amn working copy, with Throne of Bhaal only if you own and installed it. Enhanced Edition files and the trivial demo do not supply the original edition. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files.

setup.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
setup.instruction: For Windows x64, use the official SourceForge archive with its plugins, scripts and configuration. Its v0.9.5 ZIP is named gemrb-win32-v0.9.5.zip and contains a 64-bit player. The player needs the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime. Give this game its own configuration: GamePath points to a separate complete working copy of the installed original; GameType=bg2. Use the configuration supplied with your actual build rather than leaving @...@ development-template placeholders. Register gemrb.exe with the complete GemRB installation as working directory and two literal argument lines, -c then the absolute path to this game’s configuration.

setup.title: Keep the actual original and player data
setup.instruction: Choose a dedicated empty private CachePath for this game: GemRB clears that directory, so it must never be your originals, saves or profile root. SavePath is the parent containing save/, not save/ itself. Keep a separate SavePath per game.

setup.title: Choose the upstream Linux build
setup.instruction: Use the official x86-64 GemRB AppImage with the host libjack.so.0 library, or install org.gemrb.gemrb from Flathub on x86-64 or ARM64 Linux. Start the Flatpak normally once to create GemRB.cfg in ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/config/gemrb. For that package, copy this title’s complete original working copy to ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/data/baldurs-gate-2, and use that absolute GamePath in a separate baldurs-gate-2.cfg. Use a writable SavePath parent and an empty, dedicated CachePath under the same app’s data and cache directories. Start with flatpak run --command=gemrb org.gemrb.gemrb -c followed by the absolute config path in quotes. This passes the path to the player as one argument. Back up the sandbox config and actual saves separately. To register the standalone x86-64 AppImage, allow the downloaded file to run and select the AppImage itself in Portcove. Choose your private working folder. Enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines, then review and save the selection. If the official AppImage reports that it cannot mount, add --appimage-extract-and-run as the first separate argument. Keep -c and the config path on their own lines. Play starts the upstream player. For Flatpak, use the command above.

setup.title: Choose the upstream Mac build
setup.instruction: Use the Mac Source Ports Universal 2 DMG at https://github.com/MacSourcePorts/MSPBuildSystem/releases/tag/GemRB_0.9.5. Its v0.9.5 build uses macOS 10.15 or later on Intel and macOS 11 or later on Apple Silicon. GemRB’s SourceForge release directory also offers separate Intel and Apple Silicon builds. Keep the bundle complete. Use this game’s own configuration and point GamePath to the prepared original game folder. Keep this title’s saves, config and working data together when replacing the bundle. To register the Mac Source Ports bundle, copy the complete gemrb.app from the DMG and open it normally once. Select gemrb.app/Contents/MacOS/gemrb in Portcove. Choose your private working folder, then enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines. Review the selection and choose Play.

setup.title: Add the game and manage your files
setup.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Portcove saves your selected executable, working folder and launch arguments; choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, original files and profile. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions.

setup_notes.instruction: GemRB can also write gem-*.ini into GamePath before trying SavePath, so preserve and use a working data copy; SavePath alone does not isolate original installation writes. Preserve that working copy, actual save/config locations and mods with GemRB closed before updates. Do not move saves between different games or editions.

setup.title: Prepare a separate Ballance folder

setup.title: Run the upstream player
setup.instruction: On Windows open Bin/Player.exe from the working copy. On Linux or macOS enter that game's root folder in a terminal and run ./Bin/Player. The Linux runtime needs glibc 2.43 or later. The Intel and Apple Silicon Mac runtimes need macOS 15 or later.

setup.title: Preserve the working copy
setup.instruction: Close the player and back up the working game folder, including the actual Player.ini and player data, before replacing or deleting it. Keep your original installation and prior working copy available while trying a new release.

setup.instruction: Keep permitted copies of reNut and NutStaller, and point NutStaller at your player folder. If extract-xiso is missing, its separate Get extract-xiso action downloads that tool. entries.name: Uncharted: Drakes Fortune — PS4 remaster (bc160201983 Uncharted PC port)

setup.title: Prepare this PS4 collection upstream first
setup.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. This record targets Uncharted: Drake’s Fortune within your own decrypted PS4 Nathan Drake Collection CUSA02344 folder, containing eboot.bin and sce_sys (often the uroot folder). The reviewed 0.8.0 instructions recommend your own matching1.02 update; without it most port crash fixes are skipped. setup.title: Keep the complete matching package
setup.instruction: Keep Uncharted Launcher.exe with the complete python, launcher, tools, gow3_pc and other package directories from the same prepared Uncharted-windows package. The native starter invokes its bundled python/pythonw.exe and launcher script; it is not a standalone game. Do not select Python, the internal runtime probe, a DLL or an original PS4 game executable for this attachment. This guide obtains or executes no setup tool, original or game.

setup.title: Select the Drake’s Fortune play intent
setup.instruction: Select Uncharted Launcher.exe, use its complete extracted package directory as working directory, and set the two arguments --play u1. Review the exact selected intent, then request Play separately. The pinned launcher maps u1 specifically to eboot.bin; the native starter waits for the launcher, and direct play keeps it until its game/probe job completes. Finish any missing setup outside the attached attempt. Collection switching is an upstream feature, not independent qualification of the other titles.

setup.title: Preserve collection and per-game data
setup.instruction: Keep the whole package analysis directory, particularly analysis/uncharted-user with savedata, trophy, caches, probe.ini and probe-u1.ini, plus %APPDATA%/Uncharted Launcher/launcher.json. The selected source supports per-game save profiles and separate instance roots; retain every already established custom/instance root and original base/update folder. Do not assume that changing copies, region, profile or runtime migrates or preserves compatible saves automatically. No import, save migration, backup or external-file deletion is performed here.

setup.title: Complete updates and shutdown outside attachment
setup.instruction: Upstream owns preparation and its release updater, which replaces program files and restarts the launcher. Close the actual game and all helpers, retain independent recovery copies and complete maintenance outside an attached session, then review/relink changed executable bytes. Quit the game normally before closing its launcher: the GUI explicitly allows closing while the game continues. Its Stop path uses forced process-tree termination; that is not a save-flush or quiescence guarantee. Portcove does not adopt updater successors.

setup.title: Keep this implementation and its required notices
setup.instruction: This is the existing BilalReloaded/bc160201983 collection implementation, derived from gow3_pc/shadPS4, with documented port-specific maintenance; it is not merged with the separate Supermedo implementation by title alone. Preserve LICENSE.txt and all licenses/ component notices, including NVIDIA terms. Runtime grants do not grant original-game rights. Upstream per-title play/performance reports and incomplete test coverage remain upstream claims; no Portcove gameplay, save/reload, installed-app or Supported acceptance is asserted. Removing registration preserves all external files; managed install/update/rollback/backup/removal are unavailable.

entries.name: Bio Menace (ReflectionHLE)
entries.summary: Play Bio Menace through ReflectionHLE with the matching original DOS game files.

setup.title: Use the matching original DOS edition
setup.instruction: Use the complete matching original DOS episode data. Episode1 has separate shareware, registered, freeware and Gold Medallion revisions; episodes2/3 have their own registered/freeware revisions. Most use BMENACE1.EXE, BMENACE2.EXE or BMENACE3.EXE, while Gold Medallion uses BM1GM.EXE. The tagged source also recognizes the BioHazard1992 beta with BHAZARD1.EXE. Keep every companion for that exact revision. The launcher lists supported sets with exact names, sizes and CRCs. BioMenace Remastered is not established as interchangeable. Select legally obtained originals without moving them; a DOS executable is input, while reflectionhle.exe is the Windows player.

setup.title: Choose a fresh managed runtime or keep your external player
setup.instruction: For a fresh Portcove-managed runtime, use Install and then explicit Play. Keep the ordinary upstream launcher: choose this entry’s exact game/version and its complete matching original-data folder there. No automatic title dispatch or original authentication by Core is promised. The managed definition passes four separate literal arguments, -datadir, ., -cfgdir, ., with the actual player's parent folder as working directory (reflectionhle.exe on Windows, reflectionhle on Linux). On Mac, the official universal app runs with the same arguments from the folder containing reflectionhle.app. Upstream creates its version-specific writable directories after accepting the originals; no setup marker or helper is fabricated. For your separate existing external player, keep the original upstream route: Extract the official Windows 64-bit ZIP and keep reflectionhle.exe, SDL3.dll and libspeexdsp-1.dll together. Select reflectionhle.exe inside its wrapper folder and use that same folder as the working directory. Leave launch arguments empty to use the game/version picker. Complete original-file selection in the upstream launcher after explicit Play. Registration does not start it; Portcove discovery runs no original EXE, helper or game.

setup.title: Preserve the shared profile and each game version
setup.instruction: Windows normally stores ReflectionHLE settings and per-version writable data beneath %APPDATA%/reflectionhle. Preserve that whole profile, your original game folders and any custom data/config/mod locations with all copies closed before changing runtimes. Several game entries share settings; version-specific writable folders remain distinct. Changing a data/config argument redirects storage and does not migrate it. Retain the working runtime for existing saves; no cross-version or cross-engine save compatibility is established.

setup.title: Keep new private progress separate from old profiles
setup.instruction: The fresh managed runtime stores ReflectionHLE configuration, controller mappings, original-location references and per-version progress in the declared paths beside the player on Windows and Linux, or beside the app bundle on Mac. It imports no AppData, DOS or existing-player saves/configuration and adopts no populated external folder. Core manages that separate runtime and its declared data through the existing install/update, retained-runtime, backup/recovery and reviewed removal contracts. Keep originals and every external profile outside it unchanged. Existing user-selected registrations retain their creating runtime and old external ownership; they are not converted by this offer. Runtime rollback does not certify save compatibility. Preserve the creating runtime and actual progress before older-version use. Customized original/data/config argument overrides require separate upstream/external handling.

setup_notes.title: Set up Android with the upstream app

setup.instruction: Use your own original PC Blood data folder, including BLOOD.RFF, SOUNDS.RFF, BLOOD.INI and its accompanying art/data. If it is not found, add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini, or in raze_portable.ini for the Portcove-managed Windows player; do not copy game files into the managed player folder, because Portcove verifies that folder. Elsewhere, you may instead place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

setup.instruction: On Windows, choose Install, then Play explicitly. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your BLOOD.RFF archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

setup.instruction: On Windows, Portcove replaces the managed runtime and preserves its declared data. Elsewhere, you and upstream replace this external player. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. entries.name: Chocolate Doom
entries.summary: Play Doom or Doom II with the original game files, or try Doom’s shareware episode.

setup.title: Set up Doom on Windows
setup.instruction: Choose the matching original Doom IWAD or one of the listed demo editions. Portcove keeps your original file and prepares a separate copy for Play. Saved games are separate for each exact IWAD. Keep the same original with its saves; select a separate setup to change editions.

setup_notes.title: Heretic and Strife on Windows
setup_notes.instruction: The official release also offers separate chocolate-heretic and chocolate-strife Windows ZIPs. Keep each player, setup utility and DLLs together in an installation you maintain. Supply the matching Heretic IWAD, or the Strife IWAD and its accompanying voice data. These upstream alternatives retain their own setup, updates and data ownership; this managed Doom entry does not convert them into managed routes.

setup_notes.title: Install a distribution package on Linux or Mac
setup_notes.instruction: Use your Linux distribution’s chocolate-doom package for all four players. Debian packages are available on x86-64 and ARM64. On Intel or Apple Silicon Mac, use brew install chocolate-doom on a supported Homebrew host. Run the matching chocolate-doom, chocolate-heretic, chocolate-hexen or chocolate-strife command. Your package manager owns updates.

setup_notes.title: Register an existing Chocolate Doom player on Linux
setup_notes.instruction: Use portcove external select-preview for chocolate-doom-family with the absolute chocolate-doom executable path, --working-directory for its folder, --arg=-iwad and a separate --arg with the absolute path to your Doom or Freedoom IWAD. Repeat those details with portcove external select and pass the preview SHA-256 to --expected-preview. Start the game with portcove exec chocolate-doom-family. Removing the registration keeps the player, IWAD and profile.

setup_notes.title: Find settings and saves
setup_notes.instruction: For a portable Windows copy, start the player in its own folder and keep the configuration and saves it writes there. On Linux the default profile is $XDG_DATA_HOME/chocolate-doom, normally ~/.local/share/chocolate-doom. On Mac it is normally ~/Library/Application Support/chocolate-doom. Preserve the actual paths if you use -config, -extraconfig or -savedir. The default per-game save folders can differ by IWAD.

setup_notes.title: Use a short save directory for Chocolate Hexen 3.1.1
setup_notes.instruction: Chocolate Hexen 3.1.1 can fail to save when the path is long. Create a writable folder with a short absolute path and start Chocolate Hexen with -savedir followed by that path. Use a different folder for the demo and full game. Before moving either, close the game and copy its whole save folder so each slot stays with its map files.

limitations: Keep saves with their creating game and runtime. Changing engines or game editions does not convert saved games.
A profile that points outside its local autoload or music-pack folders must be preserved and corrected before Play. Portcove does not rewrite existing settings.
original_requirements: Doom PC IWAD (selected original or demo editions)

entries.name: The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker / BlueWake (chrissotraidis)
entries.summary: Explore The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker / BlueWake (chrissotraidis) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.
entries.game_title: The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker

setup.title: Use the exact GameCube edition and Windows route
setup.instruction: Use your own The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker GameCube USA GZLE01 revision 0 disc image in the supported ISO/GCM representation. Wind Waker HD for Wii U and other revisions are separate contracts. The Windows release is a native x86-64 host using translated game code and a Dolphin-derived runtime; this does not establish a completely native implementation. Follow the selected upstream release or its supported owned-disc source build; do not redistribute a private game-derived build.

setup.title: Keep the complete Windows package or completed build
setup.instruction: Retain the complete BlueWake folder, BlueWake.exe, game module, DLLs, resources and notices. The inspected selected release is v0.10.0; some README/build-page links still name v0.9.0, so do not combine their files or treat that older text as a second artifact selection. Windows 10/11 x64, Direct3D 12 and the release CPU requirements apply; the normal game module uses x86-64-v3 features including AVX2, FMA and BMI2. A source build has its own Visual Studio/Clang, Python, Git, CMake and Ninja prerequisites; the packaged player and build tools are different routes.

setup.title: Add the existing native frontend
setup.instruction: Select BlueWake.exe in the complete BlueWake folder, use that containing folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the selected program, folder and arguments, then choose Play when ready and use its own disc picker. Keep the selected disc at its existing location. RVZ and other compressed formats require their separate upstream conversion/preparation; Portcove does not acquire originals, run a converter or supply keys. Preserve project, runtime, original-game and optional texture-pack rights separately.

setup.title: Preserve the active memory card and configuration
setup.instruction: Keep the whole %APPDATA%/BlueWake folder, including GZLE01.card, sram.bin, settings.ini, logs, caches, texture/mod data and existing backups. An existing portable.txt beside BlueWake.exe instead selects its adjacent user folder; preserve that marker and populated folder. Do not create a new portable marker to add the reference or assume data moves automatically. Wind Waker Recomp 0.4 can share the same Windows data root; preserve a separate copy before switching upstream builds. Renaming a Dolphin .gci to .card is not a save conversion, and Dolphin save states are not game saves.

setup.title: Keep maintenance and observations separate
setup.instruction: Close the actual game and helpers before upstream replacement, rebuild, save import or recovery. Use upstream’s documented save tools on retained copies; Portcove does not migrate or repair cards. Review/select the executable after changes. Only the selected program is observed; removing the reference preserves external files. Managed acquisition/update/backup/rollback and Supported qualification are not supplied. Upstream playability, save-survival and controller reports are not Portcove gameplay, native or real-save observations.

limitations: Keep BlueWake.exe with its complete Windows release/build and your own GameCube USA revision 0 disc. Preserve the actual %APPDATA%/BlueWake or existing portable user folder, including GZLE01.card; Wii U HD and Dolphin save states are separate.

entries.name: Mario Kart Wii / KartPad (chrissotraidis)
entries.summary: Build your own KartPad Mac app through upstream setup and keep its game data, saves and controller features.

setup.title: Prepare your Mac copy upstream
setup.instruction: On an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 14 or newer and Xcode, use the current PadMint and choose Mario Kart Wii, your own supported PAL RMCP01 revision 0 disc and This Mac. Follow KartPad's current Mac guide and game-owned build recipe. Keep completed builds and original files. The ready-made Mac releases from 0.7.9 through 0.7.13 are a legacy alternative and receive no updates; current mobile packages are not Mac players. If a tool download fails, keep certificate verification enabled and use upstream troubleshooting or its documented manual build.

setup.title: Keep the complete app and reuse your game data
setup.instruction: Move the completed KartPad app to Applications and open it using upstream macOS instructions. When it asks for game data, choose your existing matching extracted DATA folder, or copy PadMint's prepared disc folder to a location you will keep. Reuse valid remembered choices. Retro Rewind needs the exact version named by this app and its separate whole data folder; replacing mod data alone does not update translated game code. Keep upstream Data, controls, Mii and save tools.

setup.title: Use the app or optionally register its native player
setup.instruction: Opening the finished app upstream is the simplest route. To keep an existing copy in Portcove, select KartPad.app/Contents/MacOS/KartPad, keep the complete app intact, and use its Contents/MacOS folder as the working directory. Save launch details without starting it, then choose Play explicitly.

setup_notes.title: Keep your actual saves and profile recoverable
setup_notes.instruction: Before a rebuild or update, close KartPad and back up ~/Library/Application Support/KartPad, your chosen original-game files, and the whole enclosing Retro Rewind folder because it can hold saves beside the selected data. Keep ~/Library/Caches/KartPad and custom roots if needed, the current working app and your original disc. Changing player folders does not isolate the existing profile. Preserve the app and signing identity; do not uninstall or clear data to update.

setup_notes.title: Keep KartPad updates and backups upstream-owned
setup_notes.instruction: Upstream update notices do not replace the app: rebuild the compatible version, close the old app, preserve its profile and replace the app. You or upstream own updates and data backups; Portcove registration supplies no managed Update, Backup or Rollback, and removal leaves every external file untouched.

limitations: Before a rebuild or update, close KartPad and back up ~/Library/Application Support/KartPad, your chosen original-game files, and the whole enclosing Retro Rewind folder because it can hold saves beside the selected data. Keep ~/Library/Caches/KartPad and custom roots if needed, the current working app and your original disc. Changing player folders does not isolate the existing profile. Preserve the app and signing identity; do not uninstall or clear data to update.

setup.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. Supply your own Japanese Doraemon3 N3DJ revision0,16MiB big-endian .z64 ROM. The selected README identifies SHA-256 410f99bdd58795639da272c9be9d1ab8c35b61f24f7c1fb92f7e83e1069a2602. The actual native loader checks file size0x1000000 and XXH3-64 F3BFFF0C58827510; that is a compatibility check, not a demonstrated SHA-256/entitlement check of supplied data. The ROM is not included. Convert other representations and complete any upstream generation/build outside Portcove; no ROM, BIOS, compiler or helper is acquired or run by this registration.

setup.title: Select the documented direct Windows player
setup.instruction: Keep the entire creating writable Windows folder with matching DLLs, assets and notices. Place the supported .z64 beside Dora64-3.exe, choose that native executable and its containing directory, and use no arguments. Windows wmain rejects extra arguments and discovers the matching adjacent ROM; do not use the private ROM/run-directory diagnostic interface, research probes, Android package or Linux setup script. Review and consent to the exact executable/CWD/arguments, then request Play separately.

setup.title: Close the game before changing files
setup.instruction: The native entry calls the pinned runtime in-process and waits for its game/event/saving threads before returning. The documented reset restarts the game in the same window; it is not a new Core orchestration path. Upstream/user owns preparation, replacement and recovery. Close the actual player normally, keep a separate working runtime/data backup, perform upstream maintenance, then review/relink changed selected bytes. Removing registration preserves external files; Portcove offers no external update, backup, rollback, migration, deletion or cross-version save guarantee.

setup.title: Check platform and content requirements
setup.instruction: This guide concerns Windows10/11 x64 and the selected direct entry only. Linux glibc2.43 and the Android README APK versus published ZIP discrepancy remain separate. GPL3-or-later project and runtime/component terms do not grant ROM or original/extracted assets; localized wordmarks/artwork retain their own provenance and permissions. Use only actual material you are permitted to use. Upstream gameplay/autosave/translation claims are not Portcove observations.

setup_notes.title: Preserve local saves and every settings file
setup_notes.instruction: The Windows source registers the executable directory as its configuration root and names the game dora3.n64.jp with EEPROM16k storage. Preserve the complete saves/ tree, including any dora3.n64.jp.bin and temporary/backup variants, port_pc_settings.json, port_input_settings.json, legacy port-settings.json, other runtime config/mod metadata, assets, originals and existing logs/diagnostics. Upstream imports legacy settings only when new destinations are missing and leaves the legacy file. Keep all actual custom/external roots too; this Windows entry offers no new custom-root launch argument through this guide.

limitations: Selected live startup source explicitly calls itself a research frontend with no validated gameplay loop and retains a not-playable log label. The documented Windows build enables LIVE_RT64 and disables diagnostic logging by default, so that log label is compiled out; this does not establish that the underlying comment is stale or that the game is usable. dora3_pending still stops with code77 if reached; no actual reachability/failure or normal playable session was observed. Keep this source/README1.0 conflict open for exact per-port review; do not count the guide as stable/playable runtime qualification or bypass stop paths.

The selected game config identifies title0x43430016 and XDK5849; the Windows preparation document specifies the USA release, but an exact accepted disc revision/default.xbe digest is not established here. setup.instruction: Select Darkwatch.exe, its complete creating writable output/package directory and no arguments for normal Play. setup.title: Preserve upstream preparation and lifetime boundaries
setup.instruction: The selected pinned SDK plus title patch adds PrepareGameCode before the ordinary native window/game loop: it checks stale DLL targets, can launch/wait for compiler children with a progress window, then loads the generated DLL into the native program. Complete those setup/rebuild paths outside this attachment and retain a separate known-working copy before first prepared startup; if inputs/compiler/configuration change, startup may rebuild again. Ordinary ready-player execution stays in the native process. The SDK also supports Xbox quick-reboot handoff to another executable; actual title use is unqualified and successors are outside this attached-session promise. Close all actual players/compiler/helpers/successors before maintenance.

setup.title: Use permitted files and update through the project
setup.instruction: Project/SDK and compiler/third-party licenses apply to their own code and do not grant the original game/assets or arbitrary mods. Use only a completed copy, sources and components you are independently permitted to use. Upstream/user owns generation, preparation, updates, runtime replacement and recovery. Keep previous complete runtime/data separately, maintain it upstream, then review/relink changed selected bytes. Removing registration preserves every external file; no Core builder, external update/backup/rollback/migration, save conversion or deletion is offered.

setup_notes.title: Keep every creating-runtime data and diagnostic root
setup_notes.instruction: Preserve settings.toml, the whole executable-adjacent hdd/ tree including hdd/E saves and any numbered instance hdd roots, original assets/disc, generated/runtime/compiler working outputs, shader/pipeline caches, logs/compile.log, CrashDumps/, reports/ and captures/. Preserve actual XBE_CAPTURE_DIR and other established custom/external locations too; this guide does not create environment settings or assume another port’s root. First startup may create default settings; logs can be replaced on later starts, so save independent recovery/diagnostic copies before startup or replacement. No cross-version/title save compatibility or observed write/recovery safety is claimed.

setup.title: Install Colobot
setup.instruction: On Windows x64, extract the whole ZIP into one folder and run colobot.exe there. setup.title: Start or resume a mission

setup_notes.title: Find your saved data
setup_notes.instruction: On Windows, look in the colobot folder under %USERPROFILE%. On Mac, look under ~/Library/Application Support/colobot. On Linux, look under $XDG_DATA_HOME/colobot, or ~/.local/share/colobot by default. Flatpak uses ~/.var/app/info.colobot.Colobot/data/colobot.

limitations: Close Colobot before backing up or restoring its data. Keep the whole profile folder, including colobot.ini and savegame. If you set COLOBOT_SAVE_DIR or started with -savedir, back up that folder too.

entries.name: Warcraft III / OpenRealm
entries.summary: Try the upstream Warcraft III alpha with your own classic MPQ archives.

setup.title: Add your own Warcraft III files
setup.instruction: Copy war3.mpq and War3Local.mpq, plus War3x.mpq and War3xLocal.mpq for The Frozen Throne, and any loose Maps folder from your own classic Warcraft III installation into one data folder for OpenRealm. Keep your original installation separately.

setup.title: Use a copy you manage yourself
setup.instruction: Extract the upstream alpha and keep its libraries and share directory. Start openwarcraft3.exe on Windows or bin/openwarcraft3 on Linux and Intel Mac with -data followed by the quoted path to your Warcraft III files, then -tft for The Frozen Throne or -roc for Reign of Chaos. Linux needs SDL2, glibc 2.38 or later and your distribution’s OpenGL, VA-API, VDPAU and OpenCL loader libraries. The Intel Mac executable needs macOS 15 or later and SDL2 compatibility libraries under /usr/local/opt/sdl2-compat.

setup.title: Use the publisher’s x86-64 Flatpak
setup.instruction: On Linux you can install the packaged OpenRealm Flatpak with the publisher’s instructions and the Freedesktop 25.08 runtime. Open it and select your Warcraft III folder through the file chooser. Choose whether to add an optional Steam shortcut when asked.

setup_notes.title: Keep the profile before replacing the player
setup_notes.instruction: Keep config.cfg, autoexec.cfg and saves from %APPDATA%/warcraft-3 on Windows or $XDG_DATA_HOME/warcraft-3 on Linux and Mac (usually ~/.local/share/warcraft-3). Keep any explicit -config location and the share/warcraft-3 fallback if used. Flatpak saves and its selected folder setting live in the Flatpak app profile.

setup_notes.title: Keep a separate copy's data setting in mind
setup_notes.instruction: OpenRealm saves the data folder it last used in config.cfg in the shared profile. After a run with -data data, a Windows copy started without -data looks for that relative data folder instead of searching for a Warcraft III installation; pass -data with your own folder for that copy. If the profile folder cannot be written, OpenRealm keeps config.cfg and saves under share/warcraft-3 beside the program instead.

limitations: This guide covers Warcraft III. The alpha package also includes development resources for other Blizzard games.

The Windows alpha includes SDL2, libepoxy and zlib libraries without their licence notices. The Windows and Linux alphas include the Epic Online Services SDK with the publisher’s online-service configuration for optional online play.

setup.title: Prepare the shared launcher and this game
setup.instruction: Extract the complete official Preview package for your system: CPS2Recomp-windows-x64.zip, CPS2Recomp-linux-x86_64.tar.gz, or the universal CPS2Recomp-macOS.zip with CPS-2 Recomp.app. Keep cps2recomp-launcher (cps2recomp-launcher.exe on Windows), every game program and all packaged companions together. Run the upstream launcher deliberately, choose your ROM folder or this game’s exact set, then finish its settings before registering the player. Register the launcher for your system with the CPS2Recomp folder as working directory: cps2recomp-launcher.exe on Windows or cps2recomp-launcher on Linux. On macOS, register CPS-2 Recomp.app/Contents/MacOS/cps2recomp-launcher with Contents/MacOS as working directory. Enter two literal argument lines: --play then avsp. The launcher owns this game’s configuration and child programs; do not register a source archive, update manifest or arbitrary other game executable.

setup.title: Add the game and manage updates
setup.instruction: The project’s shared launcher checks for updates and can replace the collection after its games close. Before using its update controls, keep a copy of the working game files and profile. Add this external copy to Portcove, then choose Play separately when you are ready. Removing its registration leaves the package, originals and profiles in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or deletion for these files.

setup_notes.title: Preserve the actual game and launcher data
setup_notes.instruction: Use the launcher’s Your files / Show controls to find its folder and each game’s data folder. Windows normally stores game data under %APPDATA%/<Game>/. A portable.txt file beside the launcher selects CPS2Recomp/user/, with separate launcher and game subfolders. Close all games and launchers before copying settings, save states, board memory, custom colours, scores, soundtrack files and logs. The launcher offers the initial copy to portable mode; Portcove does not move that data. Removing portable.txt changes where future sessions store data without moving existing files. Keep both locations and the working game version until the replacement works. Save-state compatibility and importing existing data have not been confirmed.

setup_notes.instruction: For Linux ARM64, use CPS2Recomp-linux-arm64.tar.gz and run cps2recomp-launcher. On an ARM64 device running Android 9 or later, install CPS2Recomp-android.apk and use Games → Add ROM sets. Get both packages and their checksums from the upstream release page.

setup.instruction: Use your own exact arcade ROM set sfa (Europe 950727), including its game key file, from a board you own. Another region or revision does not substitute for it. Keep originals separate and unchanged. The launcher accepts the set ZIP or its files folder and checks the files by checksum; when shared files are split, keep the matching parent ZIP beside it. Portcove registration does not authenticate the set or supply copyrighted game files.

setup.title: Prepare the shared launcher and this game
setup.instruction: Extract the complete official Preview package for your system: CPS2Recomp-windows-x64.zip, CPS2Recomp-linux-x86_64.tar.gz, or the universal CPS2Recomp-macOS.zip with CPS-2 Recomp.app. Keep cps2recomp-launcher (cps2recomp-launcher.exe on Windows), every game program and all packaged companions together. Run the upstream launcher deliberately, choose your ROM folder or this game’s exact set, then finish its settings before registering the player. Register the launcher for your system with the CPS2Recomp folder as working directory: cps2recomp-launcher.exe on Windows or cps2recomp-launcher on Linux. On macOS, register CPS-2 Recomp.app/Contents/MacOS/cps2recomp-launcher with Contents/MacOS as working directory. Enter two literal argument lines: --play then sfa. The launcher owns this game’s configuration and child programs; do not register a source archive, update manifest or arbitrary other game executable.

setup.title: Add the game and manage updates
setup.instruction: The project’s shared launcher checks for updates and can replace the collection after its games close. Before using its update controls, keep a copy of the working game files and profile. Add this external copy to Portcove, then choose Play separately when you are ready. Removing its registration leaves the package, originals and profiles in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or deletion for these files.

setup_notes.title: Preserve the actual game and launcher data
setup_notes.instruction: Use the launcher’s Your files / Show controls to find its folder and each game’s data folder. Windows normally stores game data under %APPDATA%/<Game>/. A portable.txt file beside the launcher selects CPS2Recomp/user/, with separate launcher and game subfolders. Close all games and launchers before copying settings, save states, board memory, custom colours, scores, soundtrack files and logs. The launcher offers the initial copy to portable mode; Portcove does not move that data. Removing portable.txt changes where future sessions store data without moving existing files. Keep both locations and the working game version until the replacement works. Save-state compatibility and importing existing data have not been confirmed.

setup_notes.title: Linux ARM64 and Android
setup_notes.instruction: For Linux ARM64, use CPS2Recomp-linux-arm64.tar.gz and run cps2recomp-launcher. On an ARM64 device running Android 9 or later, install CPS2Recomp-android.apk and use Games → Add ROM sets. Get both packages and their checksums from the upstream release page.

setup_notes.title: Preserve this game’s profile
setup_notes.instruction: On Linux preserve ~/.d1x-rebirth. On Mac preserve ~/Library/Preferences/D1X Rebirth. Keep any D1X_REBIRTH_HOME override, original files, saves, missions and settings with the creating engine.

limitations: Keep separate player/profile copies for Descent and Descent II. entries.name: TimeSplitters 2 — Destinity13 native recompilation
entries.summary: Prepare a native Windows or Linux player from your own USA PlayStation 2 disc image.
entries.download_block_reason: Portcove downloads are paused while the complete bundle and first-start recovery are being reviewed. Use these steps for an upstream copy you already trust and are permitted to use.

setup.title: Choose your original USA PlayStation 2 disc
setup.instruction: Use an ISO from your own TimeSplitters 2 USA disc, SLUS-20314. Setup checks SHA-1 01f074637a0328dd8e4ae62ac7564548e56ee126 for SLUS_203.14 inside the ISO. This identifies the game executable inside the disc.

setup.title: Prepare on Windows x64
setup.instruction: Extract the Windows package into a new writable folder. Run TS2-Recomp.bat from that folder, choose your ISO and wait for the launcher to build the game. Choose Play when setup finishes. Keep the launcher, compiler and app folder together.

setup.title: Prepare on Linux x64
setup.instruction: Extract the Linux package into a new writable folder. With Python 3 available, run TS2-Recomp.sh, choose your ISO and wait for setup before choosing Play. The included graphics bridge requires glibc 2.34 or newer, libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.30, and the X11, udev, D-Bus, curl and zlib libraries. The graphical launcher also needs glibc 2.39 and WebKitGTK 4.1. If its dependencies are missing, the script falls back to setup and launch without automatic updates.

setup_notes.title: Preserve saves and settings
setup_notes.instruction: To move from 1.0.x to 1.1, keep the old folder and prepare the new release separately. Copy the contents of the old app/build/spielstand into the new savedata folder. Keep any separate savedata_onlineplus folder and your ts2-recomp settings under %APPDATA% on Windows or XDG_CONFIG_HOME on Linux, normally ~/.config. Keep the original ISO and working copy until you have confirmed your saves.

setup_notes.title: Use the upstream Steam Deck launcher
setup_notes.instruction: Follow the upstream Steam Deck guide in Desktop Mode, then add TS2-SteamDeck.sh as a non-Steam game. Return to Desktop Mode to use the graphical launcher for updates.

limitations: Keep the disc image, extracted game files and generated game code private. Keep a complete working copy before replacing or updating it.
Use this route with a copy you already trust and are permitted to use. The upstream launcher owns updates and may rebuild the game from your remembered ISO.

entries.name: ClayFighter63andOneThird: ClayFighter64 fusion edition (djultra64 ClayFighter64)
entries.summary: Windows x64 ClayFighter 64 fused product: 63⅓ gameplay with Sculptor's Cut donor characters, requiring both exact USA ROMs. Complete upstream asset installation first, then register clayfighter64.exe with its documented ROM and fused-asset arguments. Keep local/, probe-output/ and complete runtime dependencies. The title announcement’s source is unknown; use a complete copy you already have.
entries.download_block_reason: Portcove downloads are paused because the package’s in-game title announcement comes from an audio file of unknown origin, possibly another ClayFighter game. They can resume when upstream identifies that audio’s source or publishes a package without it.

setup.title: Supply both exact owned games
setup.instruction: This combines ClayFighter63⅓ gameplay with Sculptor's Cut donor characters; it does not recreate all of Sculptor's Cut. Supply your own ClayFighter63⅓ USA and ClayFighter:Sculptor's Cut USA ROMs. After normalization to big-endian z64, their SHA256 values must be 357f26c6cd72559c5c05e8c2df46369624630dbcb1c02b3b6f3338f6ac79af07 and 9ccebc317b7ee892be3bdc0d1c8ae46687995908ed51ebd58d6855e5e25abd7f, respectively. Keep both originals separately. Other regions, revisions and modified ROMs are unsupported. Upstream preparation handles supported byte orders or a single-ROM ZIP.

setup.title: Complete upstream asset installation
setup.instruction: Use a complete v2.1.1 Windows x86-64 copy you already have. The GPL licence for authored port code does not cover packaged branding, depicted original characters or the title announcement, whose source is unknown. On Windows 10/11 x64 with an SSSE3/SSE4.1 CPU and current Vulkan drivers, run Install Assets.vbs outside Portcove and finish asset installation. The included Python runtime checks both inputs and creates local imported files. Keep all supplied DLLs, configuration, notices and assets together.

setup.title: Select the prepared native player
setup.instruction: After successful installation, select clayfighter64.exe in the complete portable package root, set that root as working directory and use literal arguments --rom probe-output/base.z64 --sc-assets local/sc_roster/asset-image-roster.z64. These are the same native arguments used by the upstream Play wrapper. Do not select VBS/CMD/Python installers or unfinished data. The native player owns the game window and normal game loop. Saving launch details and requesting Play require separate consent.

setup.title: Keep portable custom profiles inside the game
setup.instruction: Display, native game options, P1/P2 controls and training settings live in local/settings/ by default; graphics caches live under local/cache/. The executable locates its installation from its own directory/config and changes CWD to it. Optional --data-dir or --user-data selects a profile only inside that installation; outside paths and escaping symlinks are rejected. --controls imports a profile but subsequent edits save inside the installation. Preserve every selected in-root profile, temporary/recovery copies and any custom source controls before maintenance.

setup_notes.title: Preserve imported files and settings
setup_notes.instruction: Before first prepared startup, moves or updates, close the game and keep a separate complete recovery copy of local/, probe-output/, config and all original ROMs. Imported files include probe-output/base.z64, local/sc_roster/asset-image-roster.z64, local/sc_bios/bios.bin and local/import-manifest.json. Upstream installation replaces its generated outputs; reinstallation requires both originals. Keep current player settings separate from an older runtime backup.

setup_notes.title: Keep maintenance upstream-owned
setup_notes.instruction: The player and upstream own asset extraction, runtime replacement, settings and recovery. Portcove registers the explicitly selected prepared native copy; it does not acquire the originals, run extraction, update or delete external data. Finish upstream maintenance outside a tracked session, retain a complete previous runtime and current player data, then revalidate the selected executable. Do not infer compatibility between fused data, other editions or different builds.

setup_notes.title: Respect component and edition boundaries
setup_notes.instruction: Retain the GPL authored-code licence and individual SDK/RT64/SDL/Python/Microsoft notices. NOTICE explicitly excludes the branding and supplied replacement announcement from the code licence; obtaining another full package needs an applicable independent grant for those components. The optional title announcement falls back to the original ROM audio when absent, but this guide does not prescribe modifying a package or bypassing its grants. Both-ROM fusion identity and upstream claims do not establish full gameplay or save compatibility.

limitations: Portcove downloads are paused because the title announcement audio is of unknown origin. You need your own original game files.
You can add a prepared complete copy you already have; extraction, updates and recovery remain upstream-owned.

setup.instruction: Windows normally stores saves and settings under the actual Documents/My Games/dude profile, with base/d3xp scopes. Explicit fs_savepath or mod paths can redirect writes. Before first Play on Windows, preserve both the existing Documents/My Games/dhewm3 profile and its creating runtime as well as any dude profile. If the dude profile is missing, this upstream Windows build silently copies the existing dhewm3 tree into it. A private original/runtime copy does not isolate that profile behavior. setup.title: Keep an existing prepared copy
setup.instruction: Keep the complete official package and its libraries and resources together. Register dude.exe on Windows or dude on Linux in its containing runtime folder. Review its source and licence before approving it. Supply the mod data separately. Set com_allowModDownload 0 in DUDE to disable mod-library downloads. Optional graphics packs are separate. Check the upstream renderer and hardware requirements for your chosen mode; dhewm3 test results do not apply to this fork. This is an external registration: you and upstream own its runtime replacement and all files. Removing its registration preserves those files. It does not migrate or adopt the copy into a managed installation.

Place your classic Doom 3 v1.3.1 base/pak000.pk4 through base/pak008.pk4 in matching folders. Start ./dude from the prepared directory. Preserve ~/.config/dude and ~/.local/share/dude or their XDG equivalents, plus any custom paths. DUDE can copy the legacy dhewm3 config on first run. Preserve both config trees before opening DUDE. The managed Linux x86-64 copy reads your PK4s from its own runtime and starts with its packaged modules. Use a separate upstream copy for custom paths, native mods or a custom library search path. If a managed first launch would copy a legacy profile, complete that setup in an upstream copy first.

limitations: First Play can copy an existing dhewm3 profile into a missing dude profile. Preserve both and decide before continuing.

Keep your originals and edition identity; renaming another game’s WAD does not convert it. Originals are not included or authenticated by Portcove. Use a recognized upstream installation, or deliberately copy matching files into the originals subfolder (named exactly originals) of this entry’s fresh private data folder; keep your original copies.

setup.title: Use the upstream setup and launch controls
setup.instruction: Play opens crispy-doom-setup.exe. Configure controls and use F2 Warp for single-player launch; choose the matching detected IWAD there. The main-menu launch command forwards its existing arguments. The PWAD/mod browser is not an original-IWAD browser. Keep different title entries separate. Do not switch this entry’s original edition in place: its retained runtime versions share data. Use a separate Portcove library or independently owned upstream copy for another source variant. No automatic switching or cross-variant save compatibility is established. An upstream setup exit does not establish that the game loaded or ran successfully.

setup.title: Keep the declared private data scope
setup.instruction: Portcove retains originals deliberately copied under originals, this entry’s default configuration, saves under saves, known default save locations, numbered screenshots and declared recording files. Put custom recordings under demos or use a demo-prefixed .lmp filename. Upstream may read and write its music-pack profile on Play. Music packs and custom paths outside this installation remain external and outside Portcove backups. Extra files written inside the installation outside its declared folders are outside this offered scope and can block maintenance. Keep the creating runtime, original files and actual data before changing a source variant or using an older runtime.

setup.title: Keep updates in one place
setup.instruction: Portcove manages this new official game installation and the data listed for it. It does not import an existing project profile or convert a separately registered game. Existing registered copies keep their external files and update tools. Back up those external profiles and original files separately. Automated fixture checks and reaching a setup menu do not establish original-file or gameplay compatibility.

setup_notes.title: Install the native package on Linux or Mac
setup_notes.instruction: On Debian, install the crispy-doom package through the package manager. On Mac, use the upstream-documented MacPorts port or a supported Homebrew formula. Start crispy-doom with -iwad followed by the quoted path to your own DOOM2.WAD from Doom II or DOOM2F.WAD from the French edition. Use the external package manager for replacement.

setup_notes.title: Keep the existing Crispy profile
setup_notes.instruction: Preserve the actual Crispy config, saves, demos and original IWADs. Linux normally uses ~/.local/share/crispy-doom or XDG_DATA_HOME/crispy-doom. Mac normally uses ~/Library/Application Support/crispy-doom. Keep any custom locations and the creating runtime before switching package versions. The external profile can be shared across games.

limitations: Play opens the project’s setup and launch controls. Supply your own matching original game files that you are permitted to use.

setup.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. This Windows player runs the game’s x86-64 code using a title-specific PS4 compatibility layer and Vulkan translation. It does not provide general PS4 support. Select dragons_crown_pro.exe; the updater, internal boot image, DLLs and original eboot.bin are not game players.

setup.instruction: In the game’s settings, turn Allow overlay programs Off and finish preparation. Select dragons_crown_pro.exe, use the complete extracted package folder as the working directory and enter --dcp-skip-launcher as the single argument. Review those launch details and consent, then choose Play separately. With overlays Off, the game continues in the selected process. Enabling overlays starts another process and closes the selected one, which Portcove does not track. Portcove does not lock this setting; confirm it remains Off before playing. This process behavior has not been tested through Portcove.

setup.title: Preserve all builds and the actual user tree
setup.instruction: Keep the complete game/prepared/<build> and game/image/<build> trees, original PKGs, user/dcp.ini, user/savedata, trophy data, caches and numbered logs. Retain user/keys.json if you previously configured a Trophy Key; this guide neither reads nor obtains it. Existing explicit app0/image, --user, --logs or --log selections can point elsewhere; preserve every effective root without creating overrides here. Selecting another build does not prove save compatibility or migrate data. No import, backup, rollback, credential or deletion operation is performed by this attachment.

setup.title: Complete online, overlay and update work upstream
setup.instruction: Keep online account/Friend Code, service/usage-data choices and overlay/injection tools under explicit upstream/user control; this guide does not create an account, request credentials or qualify network play. setup.instruction: Keep the GPL2-or-later licence for original project code, TRG Launcher MIT licence and all component, NVIDIA and font notices. setup.instruction: Use your own original PC Duke Nukem 3D data folder, anchored by DUKE3D.GRP. Raze recognizes retail 1.3/Atomic and specific World Tour data variants; the actual group-file identity selects the edition. Keep the accompanying original files. Console, mobile and other Raze games are not substitutes. Raze searches installed Steam/GOG copies and configured game-data folders. Reuse a recognized copy; do not duplicate it unnecessarily. If it is not found, add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini, or in raze_portable.ini for the Portcove-managed Windows player; do not copy game files into the managed player folder, because Portcove verifies that folder. Elsewhere, you may instead place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

setup.title: Choose Play in the upstream player
setup.instruction: On Windows, choose Install, then Play explicitly. Portcove downloads and verifies the official Windows ZIP, keeps the player folder together, and creates Raze’s portable configuration marker so its configuration, saves, screenshots and demos stay beside the managed player, where Portcove preserves them across updates. Raze may ask which detected game/edition to use, because the same player supports several games. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your DUKE3D.GRP archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

setup.title: Keep upstream update ownership and platform handoffs
setup.instruction: On Windows, Portcove replaces the managed runtime and preserves its declared data. A separate existing Windows copy stays yours: registering it preserves every external file and Portcove does not manage its Update, Backup or Rollback, and the normal-profile settings described below are not imported into a managed install. Elsewhere, you and upstream replace this external player. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. A native Linux build outside Flatpak uses its own profile, usually ~/.config/raze. Preserve that profile and any older ~/.raze directory before launching a replacement.

setup.title: Use Raze from Flathub on Linux
setup.instruction: Install org.zdoom.Raze from Flathub for Linux x64 or ARM64. Make sure ~/.config exists in your home directory. Keep your original files and place a complete working copy of this game's data in its own subfolder under ~/.var/app/org.zdoom.Raze/.config/raze. Open Raze and choose this game if a picker appears. Close Raze and back up its actual configuration, saves and mods before updating through Flatpak.

setup_notes.title: Keep the shared profile this game uses
setup_notes.instruction: A Portcove-managed Windows install keeps raze_portable.ini, Save, Screenshots and Demos beside the managed player and does not share or import the normal-profile locations described next. Windows normally keeps raze.ini in Documents/My Games/raze, saves under the system Saved Games/Raze folder, and screenshots in the system Screenshots/Raze folder; redirected Windows known folders can change those absolute locations. A writable raze_portable.ini outside Program Files uses the player folder with Save and Screenshots instead. Custom -config/-savedir locations remain external. Normal save roots contain game/edition subfolders. A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.
