entries.name: Dune II (Dune Dynasty)
entries.summary: Play Dune II with enhanced controls, widescreen rendering and skirmish battles.

setup.title: Put your own European Dune II v1.07 PAKs in the personal data folder before Play
setup.instruction: Follow upstream’s FILELIST.TXT. On Windows, place the original files in Dune Dynasty/data under your Windows roaming app-data folder, normally %APPDATA%. On Linux, place them in dunedynasty/data under your XDG data location, normally ~/.local/share. Settings and saves use the XDG config location, normally ~/.config/dunedynasty. Keep originals and dunedynasty.cfg outside the managed game folder.

setup.title: Finish setup before registering a prepared copy
setup.instruction: Use a permitted complete Windows Dune Dynasty copy with your own European Dune II 1.07 PAK files, following upstream’s FILELIST.TXT. Keep those data files in the prepared data directory or the actual personal Dune Dynasty/data directory used by the copy. Missing original data makes normal startup fail; attaching the engine alone does not prepare it. Optional music, soundfonts and enhancements have separate requirements and rights. The ordinary launch uses no arguments. Retain any supported arguments your prepared copy already needs and review its actual working directory. For an independent Windows ARM64 or x86 copy, use the matching upstream ZIP. The 32-bit package uses a different personal directory; follow upstream’s Windows instructions before copying the PAKs.

setup.title: Set up an independent Linux ZIP or Flatpak
setup.instruction: Choose the regular x86-64 or ARM64 ZIP for your host, keep the complete extracted tree, start dunedynasty from its containing folder and use upstream’s Linux library requirements. The regular ZIPs need glibc 2.38 and libstdc++ providing GLIBCXX_3.4.32. Copy your EU v1.07 PAKs into the working copy’s data folder or your personal Dune Dynasty data folder. For the Flatpak, install and start io.github.gameflorist.dunedynasty once to create its folders, then put the PAKs in ~/.var/app/io.github.gameflorist.dunedynasty/data/dunedynasty/data. Keep the sandbox profile and external backup separate from the regular ZIP.

setup.title: Prepare the Mac app before opening it
setup.instruction: Choose the Intel or Apple Silicon ZIP from upstream. In Finder, use Show Package Contents and copy your EU v1.07 PAKs to Contents/Resources/data. The bundle launcher checks for uppercase DUNE.PAK there before it starts the player. Keep the app intact and follow upstream’s first-open instructions under your Mac’s local policy. Back up the original files and the actual profile, normally ~/Library/Application Support/dunedynasty, before replacing the app. An existing bundle-side dunedynasty.cfg selects portable settings and saves.

setup.title: Select the prepared Windows player
setup.instruction: Select dunedynasty.exe and use its containing folder as the working directory. Leave arguments empty. Keep the complete independently permitted runtime and finish the title-specific preparation before Play.

setup_notes.title: Registration ownership and removal
setup_notes.instruction: Portcove records the selected executable, working folder and literal arguments after review. Play is separate and only the selected process is supervised. You and upstream own replacement and updates; relink changed executable bytes after reviewing them. Removing this registration preserves every external file. Managed installation, backup, rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for this external copy.

setup_notes.title: Player-data ownership
setup_notes.instruction: You and upstream own the external copy's data: the complete personal Dune Dynasty profile or the actual executable-side data and configuration of your prepared copy. Back up these locations separately; registration does not migrate or certify their compatibility.

setup_notes.title: Managed runtime ownership
setup_notes.instruction: Portcove installs and replaces its separate official runtime using the declared release rules. Existing external registrations retain their files and user/upstream ownership. Runtime rollback carries current declared data; it does not rewind saves or establish older-runtime compatibility. Gameplay and populated-save compatibility remain separate qualification. The managed copy has no declared local player data to back up. Back up the external profile separately.

limitations: Use only a copy and content you are already permitted to use. Engine licensing does not grant rights to original game assets, music, mods or bundled components.
Before updating the game, keep a copy of its working files and every location containing saved data. Choosing a different executable does not give it a separate profile.

Do not create an executable-side config merely to register the game. Preserve that whole actual profile, its save directory, configuration, original data, custom campaigns/music and the old creating runtime before replacement. Original-format save reading is not a promise that every newer save works in an older engine.

Linux and Mac screenshots and the save directory belong to the profile containing the active dunedynasty.cfg. On a regular Linux build, that is normally ~/.config/dunedynasty unless an executable-side config already selects a portable profile. Back up the actual config, save folder and original-data folder. The Flatpak has a separate sandbox profile.
Upstream and the player maintain independent copies and their profiles. Back up the actual data and configuration paths, especially if your environment redirects HOME or the XDG paths.
The Linux x86-64 ZIP needs glibc 2.38, libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.32, and the upstream Allegro, ALSA, ENet, MAD and OpenGL libraries. Keep the packaged libs folder with the player.

Back up the actual Dune Dynasty settings, saves and original data separately. Linux uses HOME to resolve relative XDG paths. Use an independent upstream copy for executable-side profiles. Real saves across versions remain unverified.

setup.title: Complete upstream migration and restarts separately

entries.name: Crash Team Racing: Nitro-Fueled (CTR-NitroFueled-PC)
entries.summary: Attach an independently permitted, prepared GetLostIn CTR Nitro-Fueled Windows installation. Its native settings launcher waits for the game runner; upstream owns PS4-data preparation, runtime replacement and the external save/cache roots.

setup.title: Prepare the correct PS4 game and update upstream
setup.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. The 0.4 Windows route documents your own CTR Nitro-Fueled PS4 CUSA13795 or CUSA14876 base game and matching 1.21 update; both documented 1.21 firmware builds are accepted by upstream. Follow its first setup outside Portcove and keep independent originals before creating its merged game folder. Its preparation uses hard links where possible: a merged tree is not an independent backup of original file contents. No original, DLC, extractor, Python helper or game is obtained or executed here.

setup.title: Keep the complete selected Windows implementation
setup.instruction: The inspected CTR-NitroFueled-PC-portable-windows.zip contains CTR-NitroFueled-PC-portable/CTR-NitroFueled-PC.exe, bin/sacredfire.exe, bundled python, scripts, DLLs and resources. The ordinary frontend is an AMD64 native Windows launcher, not the older Python launcher or a standalone game exe. Keep the whole matching package. This is the existing GetLostIn Windows adaptation of SacredFire with its own maintained Windows layer/launcher and credited upstream fixes; a common game title does not merge it with the separate online fork or qualify the parent’s Linux route.

setup.title: Select and retain the normal launcher session
setup.instruction: After upstream setup, select CTR-NitroFueled-PC.exe, use its complete extracted portable package directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review and consent to the selected launch details, then choose Play separately. This opens the upstream launcher; request its Play only when ready. The native frontend waits for its Python runner, which waits for sacredfire.exe. The runner loops over its own Apply and restart exit code, retaining the ordinary waiting chain. Quit the actual game before closing the frontend; its Stop game and quit action forcibly terminates the job and is not a save-flush guarantee. Portcove has not tested this launch-and-quit sequence.

setup.title: Preserve the actual data and hard-link sources
setup.instruction: Keep the whole package user tree with savedata, cache and trophies, the separate backups and DLC directories, launcher.ini, bbport.ini, patches.json, logs and the full prepared game view. Keep the original base/update/DLC sources independently too. The runner normally uses user for saves/cache, while an established BB_USER_DIR or other data/mod/config override can select additional external roots; preserve every effective location. Do not edit a hard-linked merged source as though it were an isolated disposable copy. This guide performs no save import, migration, backup or deletion.

setup.title: Leave replacement and recovery with upstream
setup.instruction: Complete upstream updates, first preparation, repairs and source-root changes outside an attached session. Close all actual players/helpers before replacing files, keep independent recovery copies, then review/relink changed executable bytes. Normal waiting/restart source paths do not establish observed forced-stop cleanup or save consistency. Portcove does not own the mutable upstream runtime, merged originals, backups or external player data. Removing registration preserves all external files.

setup.title: Retain permission and platform limits
setup.instruction: Preserve GPL 2-or-later and all packaged third-party/NVIDIA/font notices; these grants do not grant original-game or DLC rights. Upstream playable race/audio/controller/save reports remain upstream claims; shader stalls and experimental upscaling/frame-generation/ultrawide limits remain. setup.title: Open the generated player
setup.instruction: After setup succeeds, open the player for your original. gticlub2 for JAB or gticlub2ea for EAA. On Windows the player has an .exe extension. Open the same player on later launches. Use Options for settings. The --classic option starts the arcade mode.

setup_notes.title: Keep saves when replacing the package
setup_notes.instruction: Keep the NVRAM saves and settings beside the generated player, including its separate enhanced and classic saves. Back up that folder before replacing the release, then run the upstream setup again for the new version. Portcove does not replace the generated runtime or back up its data.

setup_notes.title: Use the upstream command line
setup_notes.instruction: For the default release variant, run viper-setup --prepare --roms with your original-files folder followed by gticlub2. Watch the progress lines and wait for success. Then viper-setup --play gticlub2 starts the generated player and returns its exit status. Exit code 66 means the upstream setup has no built game for that variant.

limitations: The release package contains a builder. You supply the original game files and board BIOS.

setup.title: Preserve both mod layouts before migration
setup.instruction: Before startup, separately back up the complete exe-local mods/ tree, including packages/, bundled/, installed/ and state.toml. The pinned runtime migrates legacy mods/packages/<id>/<version> into mods/installed/<id>/<version>, preferring a rename then recursive copy fallback. It deletes legacy versions already present in bundled/ or installed/, and removes the remaining legacy packages tree when its migration reports no stranded version/error. Do not rely on duplicate legacy folders or unrecognized loose files as recovery copies; preserve them outside that tree before starting. Build-staged bundled mods and user-installed mods remain upstream-owned.

setup.title: Keep one replacement owner
setup.instruction: Upstream and the player own tools, generation, rebuilds, updates, game settings, cards and recovery. Portcove only registers your selected completed native copy; it does not acquire originals, build or replace the runtime or delete its external files. Finish upstream maintenance outside a tracked session, retain a complete recovery copy, then revalidate the selected executable. Recover runtime and current player data deliberately rather than rewinding saves with an old build.

setup.title: Keep title and permission limits

entries.name: Icewind Dale II (GemRB)
entries.summary: Set up Icewind Dale II through its upstream gemrb player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.

setup.title: Use this original game and edition
setup.instruction: Use a complete installed original Icewind Dale II working copy. Icewind Dale I, Enhanced Edition and the included trivial demo are different inputs. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files.

setup.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
setup.instruction: For Windows x64, use the official SourceForge archive with its plugins, scripts and configuration. Its v0.9.5 ZIP is named gemrb-win32-v0.9.5.zip and contains a 64-bit player. The player needs the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime. Give this game its own configuration: GamePath points to a separate complete working copy of the installed original; GameType=iwd2. Use the configuration supplied with your actual build rather than leaving @...@ development-template placeholders. Register gemrb.exe with the complete GemRB installation as working directory and two literal argument lines, -c then the absolute path to this game’s configuration.

setup.title: Keep the actual original and player data
setup.instruction: Choose a dedicated empty private CachePath for this game: GemRB clears that directory, so it must never be your originals, saves or profile root. SavePath is the parent containing save/, not save/ itself. Keep a separate SavePath per game.

setup.title: Choose the upstream Linux build
setup.instruction: Use the official x86-64 GemRB AppImage with the host libjack.so.0 library, or install org.gemrb.gemrb from Flathub on x86-64 or ARM64 Linux. Start the Flatpak normally once to create GemRB.cfg in ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/config/gemrb. For that package, copy this title’s complete original working copy to ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/data/icewind-dale-2, and use that absolute GamePath in a separate icewind-dale-2.cfg. Use a writable SavePath parent and an empty, dedicated CachePath under the same app’s data and cache directories. Start with flatpak run --command=gemrb org.gemrb.gemrb -c followed by the absolute config path in quotes. This passes the path to the player as one argument. Back up the sandbox config and actual saves separately. To register the standalone x86-64 AppImage, allow the downloaded file to run and select the AppImage itself in Portcove. Choose your private working folder. Enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines, then review and save the selection. If the official AppImage reports that it cannot mount, add --appimage-extract-and-run as the first separate argument. Keep -c and the config path on their own lines. Play starts the upstream player. For Flatpak, use the command above.

setup.title: Choose the upstream Mac build
setup.instruction: Use the Mac Source Ports Universal 2 DMG at https://github.com/MacSourcePorts/MSPBuildSystem/releases/tag/GemRB_0.9.5. Its v0.9.5 build uses macOS 10.15 or later on Intel and macOS 11 or later on Apple Silicon. GemRB’s SourceForge release directory also offers separate Intel and Apple Silicon builds. Keep the bundle complete. Use this game’s own configuration and point GamePath to the prepared original game folder. Keep this title’s saves, config and working data together when replacing the bundle. To register the Mac Source Ports bundle, copy the complete gemrb.app from the DMG and open it normally once. Select gemrb.app/Contents/MacOS/gemrb in Portcove. Choose your private working folder, then enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines. Review the selection and choose Play.

setup.title: Add the game and manage your files
setup.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Portcove saves your selected executable, working folder and launch arguments; choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, original files and profile. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions.

setup_notes.title: Preserve working data across updates
setup_notes.instruction: GemRB can also write gem-*.ini into GamePath before trying SavePath, so preserve and use a working data copy; SavePath alone does not isolate original installation writes. Preserve that working copy, actual save/config locations and mods with GemRB closed before updates. Do not move saves between different games or editions.

limitations: GemRB clears its cache directory. Use a dedicated private CachePath, separate from original files, saves and profile roots.

entries.name: Mario Party 6 (Starlit Party)
entries.summary: Attach an independently permitted, prepared Starlit Party Windows player for your own Mario Party 6 USA disc. Preserve its actual working-directory saves and content root; limited minigame coverage and title-specific launcher/font permission scope remain explicit.

setup.title: Prepare your own USA disc upstream
setup.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use. Finish upstream preparation outside Portcove, keep independent originals and recovery copies. No original, helper, compiler or game is obtained or executed by this guide. Use your own Mario Party 6 USA GameCube disc image or matching extracted disc tree. Complete the supported upstream content import and configuration first, retaining the independent original and any selected external content root. Another region or Mario Party game is not admitted by the shared engine. The Windows native player, Android APK and browser/iPhone experience are different artifacts, not a shared native-platform qualification.

setup.title: Keep the complete Windows package
setup.instruction: The inspected official 0.5.0 Windows ZIP contains AMD64 mp6native.exe, renderer libraries, res/ and notices. Keep the complete extracted package. The selected native entry launches the UI and calls GameMain within the same process; do not select a GameCube executable, disc image, browser bundle, Android package or build script. Package presence and source review do not establish complete imports, dependencies or Windows gameplay.

setup.title: Attach the prepared player
setup.instruction: Select mp6native.exe, use its complete extracted package folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review and consent to the selected launch details, then choose Play separately, then use the upstream player UI with its already prepared content. Working directory matters: Windows saves are deliberately relative to it. Complete any missing import/preparation outside the attached attempt. Quit the actual game normally; forced termination is not a save-flush guarantee.

setup.title: Preserve actual saves and content configuration
setup.instruction: Keep mp6_config.json beside the executable, the saves/ directory relative to the established working directory, memory-card GCIs, states, logs, renderer caches and the selected external content tree. Preserve old working-directory save roots if they differ from the package directory; do not change CWD without reviewing that effect. Upstream states require the same linked build, while GCIs are durable game saves; neither establishes observed restore compatibility. This guide performs no move, migration, backup or deletion.

setup.title: Retain title-specific permission and font evidence
setup.instruction: Keep docs/PARTYBOARD_PROVENANCE.md, all author credits, res/fonts/LICENSES.txt and runtime/component notices. The selected upstream publicly records its maintainer’s 2026-09-12 confirmation of permission to redistribute the adapted Partyboard launcher and N64 Party font with this MP6 release. It explicitly does not claim a public general license for those foreign materials; this guide does not reuse that confirmation for another project or artifact. Other fonts have separate OFL/Apache terms. Original game code/assets still require a copy you are independently permitted to use.

setup.title: Maintain the external copy and limited scope
setup.instruction: Quit the game normally before changing files; forced termination may not finish saving. After an upstream update, relink and review the changed executable. Removing the registration leaves all external files in place; Portcove does not install, update, roll back, back up or delete this copy. Upstream reports only 49 of 81 minigames playable, with unsupported board minigames skipped after a notice. Portcove has not confirmed minigames, boards, microphone support, saving or gameplay on Windows or other platforms.

limitations: Preserve working-directory saves and exact USA content. Partial minigame coverage and this release’s limited launcher/font permission record do not grant broader support or reuse rights.

setup.title: Finish the supported European game setup
setup.instruction: Use your own inFamous European PS3 BCES00220 files and complete the upstream Windows setup, translation and build before adding the player. An already decrypted supported folder avoids a key-input route; encrypted images have their separate owner-supplied requirements. This guide provides no keys, decryption or game data. setup.title: Keep the complete prepared installation
setup.instruction: Retain the full completed port directory, its native inFamous.exe launcher, installer/launch.txt, build-install/inFamousRecomp.exe, the prepared game/ELF, libraries, settings and notices. The producer writes executable, working-directory, argument and environment values into launch.txt. The normal launcher reads those values; selecting the bare game without its published context is not an equivalent shortcut. Keep project/runtime/compiler/component terms separate from original game rights and do not share private translated outputs.

setup.title: Add the native upstream launcher
setup.instruction: Select the completed inFamous.exe in its existing port directory, use that directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the selected program, folder and arguments, then choose Play when ready. Its native launcher supplies the producer-written launch configuration and environment. Portcove observes that launcher only; it can report the launch finished after handoff while inFamousRecomp.exe and helpers still run. Use the game’s own controls to quit and do not interpret the launcher’s exit as full-game completion.

setup.title: Preserve the current saves and launch configuration
setup.instruction: Keep the whole existing port, installer/launch.txt, settings.ini, all original/generated content and gamedata/. Default saves are under gamedata/dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata relative to the configured port working directory; retain all profiles, trophies and related data as present. Existing SAVEDATA_ROOT and other producer/user path overrides must remain intact. Do not transplant launch.txt into a different layout, reset populated settings or merge saves merely to add the launcher. No save conversion, migration, backup or restore is performed.

setup.title: Leave updates and recovery upstream
setup.instruction: Close the actual game and helpers before upstream replacement, rebuild, repair or recovery, even if Portcove’s activity has finished. Upstream owns imports, build tools, runtime replacement and launch configuration; review/select the current launcher again after changes. Early-release PPU/SPU, rendering and campaign claims do not establish gameplay/controller/real-save acceptance here. Removing the library reference preserves all external files. No managed installation/update/backup/rollback, full-session tracking or Supported qualification is supplied.

limitations: Select the completed inFamous.exe launcher and preserve installer/launch.txt plus its full port/data directory. Its handoff can outlive Portcove’s activity; close the actual game/helpers before upstream changes. The setup EXE and a context-free bare runtime are separate routes.

setup.instruction: Supply your own legally owned Xbox 360 XBLA Banjo-Tooie package, not an N64 ROM. Its generated source and generated/rexglue.cmake are intentionally absent from Git: finish the pinned SDK codegen against that manifest before the documented CMake configure/build target banjotooie. setup.instruction: Select the completed banjotooie.exe build with its containing output folder as the working folder, retaining rexruntime.dll and every companion staged by the build. The selected native app owns its Windows message loop and waits for the guest game; it is a different entry from the outer Banjo-Tooie.exe launcher. That packaged launcher starts a child then exits, so do not use it for a tracked Portcove session or select a private PyInstaller extraction path. Saving launch details and Play are separate actions.

setup.instruction: Upstream/player owns runtime replacement and the extracted originals. For this direct native app the default player-data root is Documents/banjotooie and its cache is under that root; the executable-side banjotooie.toml is separate. Explicit --user_data_root, --cache_path or opt-in --update_data_root values select other roots. Retain the exact chosen arguments and preserve all active roots before changing builds. The packaged launcher’s BanjoTooie-Data/saves override is a different layout and is not automatically inherited or migrated by a direct build. Portcove does not promise external-save backup, rollback, compatibility or deletion.

limitations: This guide follows upstream source instructions. Portcove has not run original-data preparation, generation, compilation or the game, or checked the resulting build, dependency compatibility, files, saves or source correspondence. setup.instruction: The reviewed release has no Linux package. Use the upstream source with a C11 compiler, CMake 3.24 or newer and SDL3 development files. setup.instruction: Use a C11 compiler, CMake 3.24 or newer and the macOS SDL3 framework from SDL’s official development package. Keep SDL3.framework in a stable folder. Replace both paths with your actual framework locations. Build on the Mac you will use, so the player matches Intel or Apple Silicon. Keep the framework folder in place after building. The Windows ZIP and launcher are not used. Native Mac game startup and saving have not been tested.

setup.instruction: On Windows, choose jsport.exe as the existing installation; on Linux or Mac, choose the built jsport. Choose the player’s containing directory as the working directory. Add --game-dir and your writable Game copy as two separate arguments. Review the selected player, folder and arguments, then choose Play. The separate upstream launcher can stay open or close while its game continues.

setup_notes.instruction: Back up JS.CFG, js_save.000 through js_save.009 and any MUSIC folder with your working game data. Copy %APPDATA%/JetStrike/settings.ini as well. entries.name: Little Big Adventure 2 / LBA2 Classic Community
entries.summary: Play the classic Little Big Adventure 2 with the LBA2 Classic Community engine.

setup.title: Choose your classic game data
setup.instruction: Use the original PC retail files or the classic installation from GOG or Steam. When the engine asks, choose the folder containing LBA2.HQR and keep the other game files and media directories together. In a store installation, look for the classic data under Common or CommonClassic. For an owned disc image, follow the publisher’s game-data guide.

setup.title: Open the package for your desktop
setup.instruction: On Windows x64, extract the ZIP and run lba2cc.exe. On Linux x86-64 or ARM64, choose the matching AppImage, make it executable and open it with FUSE available. The matching TAR.GZ avoids FUSE and needs glibc 2.38 or later. On Intel or Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 11 or later, open the universal DMG, copy the app to Applications and follow its first-run instructions.

setup_notes.title: Set up the Android release
setup_notes.instruction: Use the publisher’s arm64-v8a or armeabi-v7a APK on Android 7 or later and follow its Android guide to place your original data. The shared lba2cc folder requires Android’s All Files Access on Android 11 or later. Check the active save folder in the startup log. With shared storage, back up lba2cc/user/LBA2. App-owned fallback folders can be erased on uninstall, so verify a separate copy of your saves before uninstalling.

setup_notes.title: Keep your saves when changing packages
setup_notes.instruction: With the game closed, copy Twinsen/LBA2 under %APPDATA% on Windows, $XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share on Linux, or ~/Library/Application Support on Mac. If you chose --user-dir or LBA2_USER_DIR, copy that directory with its profiles. If you added portable.txt, copy User/LBA2 beside the engine. Keep originals and profiles separate from replacement package files.

limitations: These stable packages need the classic retail data. The 1997 demo has different game files and needs its own engine build.

entries.name: Little Fighter 2 / LF2 Port

setup.title: Prepare a separate game copy
setup.instruction: Use the original developers' Little Fighter 2 v2.0a installer. Extract it with the upstream tagged helper into a new writable folder, or copy a complete already-extracted v2.0a tree. Keep the original installer and any original extracted tree separately.

setup.title: Set up the Linux x64 AppImage
setup.instruction: Make LF2-Port-x86_64.AppImage executable. Put the working tree in a folder named game beside it, or open the upstream picker and choose lf2.exe from the complete working tree. To import a complete ZIP, choose ZIP archive in the file-type menu if the picker starts with the executable filter.

setup.title: Add the working Linux player
setup.instruction: Once the AppImage works on your system, select it in Portcove and keep its containing folder as the start folder. Save the launch details, then choose Play. Removing the registration leaves the working tree in place.

setup_notes.title: Preserve the selected game and profile
setup_notes.instruction: Keep the working game tree and the lf2-port profile under XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config. The port stores a ZIP import under game-import in its profile. Preserve that selected tree, lf2.cfg and any recordings or mods that you add.

setup_notes.title: Check Linux and other platform options
setup_notes.instruction: Linux v0.1.2 has an x64 AppImage. Launch it with APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 if FUSE is unavailable. Music needs ffmpeg on PATH. The release also offers a separate ARM64 Android 7 or later debug preview with a folder or ZIP import. macOS uses the upstream source build. The original Windows game is a separate player.

limitations: This upstream player includes translated original game code. The original game and its data remain under the original developers' terms.

Use a separate writable working tree. The game can write files inside it as well as in the port profile. Back up both locations before replacing the player. A successful new ZIP import replaces the previous imported tree, so preserve its recordings and changes first.

setup.instruction: Use the Little Fighter 2 v2.0a installer offered by the original developers at lf2.net. Keep it as a file. OpenLF2 verifies the file and reads its game data without running the original installer.

setup.instruction: Run the OpenLF2 v1.2.0 setup program for your Windows architecture. If you already have the original, clear the Download the original Little Fighter 2 installer task. OpenLF2 can read your file from %APPDATA%\OpenLF2 or through the --installer argument. Add the installed openlf2.exe to Portcove after confirming it starts.

On macOS 13 or later, extract and keep the complete Intel or Apple Silicon app. Keep the original in the OpenLF2 profile, or launch the player with --installer followed by its absolute path.

setup.title: Add a working desktop copy
setup.instruction: Select the existing native player and keep its working directory. If it needs explicit paths, enter --installer and the absolute path to the original as two arguments. Use --config-dir and the creating profile's absolute path as two more arguments if you already use that override. Save the launch details, then choose Play. Removing the registration leaves the player and its profile where you put them.

setup_notes.title: Find the desktop profile
setup_notes.instruction: The upstream player uses the operating system's OpenLF2 data folder. An explicit --config-dir keeps config.json and the recording directory in that selected folder. Keep the original separately and retain any .lfr recordings and mods you add.

setup_notes.title: Choose an upstream package
setup_notes.instruction: The v1.2.0 release includes Windows x86, x64 and ARM64 installers, Linux x86, x64 and ARM64 AppImage and Debian packages, and separate Intel and Apple Silicon Mac apps. Android previews cover ARM32, ARM64, x86 and x64 on API 21 or later. Choose the package for the device's architecture. setup.instruction: Run the upstream Windows Installer EXE. Choose a separate TRX folder and the packs you want. Point it to your supported Steam, GOG or disc installation for each game. In Portcove, select the installed TRX.exe and use its containing folder as the start folder.

Follow the upstream file map to copy your own original files into the correct games/<game-id>/ folders. Select TRX.exe and its containing folder. Keep the complete extracted package with the player.

setup.instruction: The universal TRX 1.12 Mac package requires macOS 14 or later on Intel and Apple Silicon. Mount the DMG, copy TRX.app to Applications, and open the installed app once as described by upstream. Use the upstream manual setup guide to place the original game files under the corresponding Contents/Resources/games/<game-id>/ folders. Open TRX.app from Applications to play.

setup_notes.instruction: Keep a backup of your original game files, cfg, saves, screenshots and any custom profile directories before replacing the runtime. Preserve saves, screenshots, configuration and any paths selected through TRX_DIR or the documented TRX path overrides before switching your registration.

entries.name: Mage Bros. / Mage Bros. Native

setup.title: Keep the original Mage Bros. files together
setup.instruction: Get the freeware 2.0 release from Saito Games, using the publisher link in the setup guide. Keep MageBros.exe and Music01.mid through Music06.mid together. The native engine checks the original executable before reading its game data.

setup.title: Start the native Windows engine
setup.instruction: Extract the Windows x64 package into a writable folder. Run MageBrosNative.exe with --game followed by the quoted path to the original MageBros.exe. Use Windows 10 or 11 with OpenGL 3.3. If Windows reports missing MSVCP140.dll or VCRUNTIME140.dll, install Microsoft’s Visual C++ v14 x64 Redistributable.

setup_notes.title: Keep settings and progress before replacing the engine
setup_notes.instruction: Close the game and copy magebros_native.ini and your screenshots from the engine directory. Back up %APPDATA%/MageBrosNative/saves/original or the folder you chose in save_path. Keep the original executable and music in their own folder.

setup_notes.title: Build for Apple Silicon or a Linux handheld
setup_notes.instruction: The publisher’s build guide covers Apple Silicon on macOS 12 or later and the R36S Linux handheld. The Apple Silicon build stores settings and saves under ~/Library/Application Support/MageBrosNative. The R36S needs the original files and a General MIDI SoundFont for music. The tagged release provides a ready-made package for Windows.

limitations: The upstream package includes reconstructed Mage Bros. and DirectX framework code. The MIT grant covers the port’s own code. Rights to the reconstructed code remain with their original owners.
Mage Bros. Native keeps its own progress. Start a new native save if you previously played the original game.

setup.title: Prepare a writable copy of your original game folder
setup.instruction: Use your own Magic Ball 2 or Smash Frenzy 2 installation. Keep its original data together, including any .pak or .dat archives. The engine writes player files in the game-data folder.

setup.instruction: If you have permission to use the Windows x64 OpenMB2 package, put OpenMB2.exe and the OpenMB2 folder in your writable game folder. Run OpenMB2.exe. The upstream guide also gives --game and --overrides options for keeping the engine files separate.

entries.game_title: Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter

setup.title: Get the matching arcade files
setup.instruction: Use your own Marvel Super Heroes Vs. Street Fighter (Europe 970625) arcade ROM set (`mshvsf`).

setup.title: Set up the game in the collection
setup.instruction: Extract the complete package for your system. Open CPS-2 Recomp and select the ROM folder on its Games page. Pick the game and press Play.

setup.title: Start the prepared game again
setup.instruction: Choose Play in CPS-2 Recomp. On desktop, a frontend can call the collection launcher with two arguments, `--play` and `mshvsf`. Open the launcher without arguments to change the ROM folder or settings.

setup_notes.title: Linux ARM64 and Android
setup_notes.instruction: For Linux ARM64, use CPS2Recomp-linux-arm64.tar.gz and run cps2recomp-launcher. On an ARM64 device running Android 9 or later, install CPS2Recomp-android.apk and use Games → Add ROM sets. Get both packages and their checksums from the upstream release page.

setup_notes.title: Find saves and update the collection
setup_notes.instruction: Use Your files → Show in the launcher to find the actual launcher and game folders. With portable.txt beside the launcher or Mac app, the collection uses user/ there. Keep your settings, saves and the working package before replacing it. The shared launcher offers updates. Leave its files together and manage them outside Portcove.

limitations: This upstream package is a prerelease. Portcove has package evidence for this version. Individual gameplay and save restoration are unverified.

entries.summary: Run Master of Magic with ReMoM using the original game data from your own DOS installation.

setup.title: Choose the engine archive
setup.instruction: Extract the full Windows ZIP and open ReMoM.exe. On Linux, extract the tarball and run ReMoM with SDL2 and SDL2_mixer installed.

setup.title: Point ReMoM at your own Master of Magic files
setup.instruction: ReMoM looks for version 1.31 files in the usual GOG, Steam and CD install locations. If it cannot find them, follow the upstream guide to set game_data in ReMoM.ini, or put the original .LBX files next to the executable. Open the same program again to play.

setup_notes.title: Keep the working save folder
setup_notes.instruction: The default save folder is %APPDATA%/ReMoM on Windows or ~/.local/share/ReMoM on Linux. The program can copy SAVE1.GAM through SAVE9.GAM from your original on first run. Keep the working copies before replacing the engine with a newer upstream release.

limitations: Portcove does not back up your ReMoM saves.

entries.name: Master of Orion (1oom (vanilla branch))
entries.summary: Research listing. Upstream route: Native recreation with original v1.3 LBX input and Windows RC package. Limits: Default branch warns no longer developed; select vanilla branch/current lineage and heed save compatibility. Upstream platforms: Windows release-candidate package on vanilla lineage; desktop source builds documented. Selected Windows CPU architecture unknown in frozen evidence; discontinued default branch differs. Original data: Legally own Master of Orion version 1.3 and supply its original LBX files. This 1oom target does not establish compatibility with a different original-game version; separately preserve its documented save-compatibility limitations. Portcove setup/gameplay not verified.

setup.title: Choose the actual vanilla RC5 lineage
setup.instruction: Use a permitted completed Windows copy of the reviewed 1oom vanilla-RC5 beta/testing package and your own Master of Orion version 1.3 LBX data. The exact tag and current master-vanilla-beta-RC5 branch resolve to a956a6f73f75e6cd26b701afcd04bd4973650520. The discontinued default branch/latest v1.11.9 and the separately referenced newer SourceCraft project do not inherit this guide. A provider prerelease flag of false does not remove the beta/RC/testing scope. No version pin or automatic managed replacement of this lineage is offered.

setup.title: Select the native graphical player
setup.instruction: Select the prepared graphical 1oom_classic_sdl2.exe (or the actual prepared SDL1 graphical variant), keeping the complete companion DLLs and chosen MOO data directory. Do not select lbxview, saveconv, the command-line demonstration, a DOS executable or emulator. Retain established -data ABS and -user ABS as separate literal arguments when configured; they select distinct data and user roots.

setup.title: Preserve original-format slots and configuration
setup.instruction: Preserve the whole creating runtime, all LBX originals, CONFIG.MOO and every SAVE*.GAM or 1oom_save*.bin slot in the actual user root. Selected Windows source defaults that root to the working directory, not an invented literal User subfolder; -user can redirect it. Original-format saves are enabled by default and use the original MOO slot names, so running inside the original installation can overwrite those existing slots. Keep an independent recoverable copy before running/changing engines. Source support for a format is not observed backward compatibility or permission to migrate saves.

setup.title: Review the prepared player and launch details
setup.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools, then start and quit the permitted copy you intend to add. Keep its game executable, working folder and supported launch arguments. Review those details in Portcove and agree to launch them, then choose Play separately. Adding a copy does not confirm its original game files, gameplay or save compatibility.

setup.title: Retain upstream replacement and external ownership
setup.instruction: Close every running copy of the game before changing files. Keep the working game version and every original-file, profile and data location it uses. Update it with the project’s tools, then review and select the changed executable in Portcove. You manage setup, replacement, file changes, data migration and recovery. Portcove monitors the process you selected; it does not restrict file access or prevent other copies from running. Removing the registration leaves external files in place. This route does not offer Portcove downloads, setup, updates, backups, rollback, data migration or external-file deletion.

limitations: Use only a copy and components you are already permitted to use. Engine licensing does not grant original-game, music, mod, middleware or redistribution rights.
Before changing versions, keep a copy of the working game and every data and profile folder it uses. Another executable may use those same folders.

entries.name: MDK / SDL engine (nemo22)
entries.summary: Explore MDK / SDL engine (nemo22) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

setup.title: Prepare your original game on Windows
setup.instruction: On Windows, keep your own original MDK installed in a supported default GOG or Steam location; the player detects it. If it is elsewhere, follow upstream’s Running instructions to create mdk_paths.cfg beside mdk_sdl.exe and name the original folder in its [paths] mdk setting. The original files stay external and are read at runtime. The ZIP contains the native player and SDL3.dll; no game compilation or separate installer is required.

setup.title: Set up MDK on Linux
setup.instruction: On x86-64 Linux, Portcove can install and update the official mdk-linux-x64.tar.gz player. Linux has no default game-location detection, so create mdk_paths.cfg beside mdk_sdl and name your complete original installation in its [paths] mdk setting; Portcove does not pass MDK_DATA_DIR to the game. For an ARM64 copy you maintain, choose mdk-linux-arm64.tar.gz from the stable releases, keep libSDL3.so beside mdk_sdl, and point MDK_DATA_DIR or the [paths] mdk entry in mdk_paths.cfg at your original installation. Use a Vulkan driver. The inspected v1.2.6 x86-64 player needs glibc 2.43 or later and its ARM64 sibling needs glibc 2.38 or later.

setup.title: Set up MDK on an Apple silicon Mac
setup.instruction: Portcove can install and update the official mdk-osx-arm64.zip player. Create mdk_paths.cfg beside mdk_sdl and name your complete original installation in its [paths] mdk setting; Portcove does not pass MDK_DATA_DIR to the game. Keep libSDL3.dylib beside mdk_sdl. The inspected v1.2.6 package requires macOS 12 or later with Metal.

setup.title: Set up MDK on Android
setup.instruction: Choose mdk-android.apk from the stable releases. The inspected v1.2.6 APK needs 64-bit Android 8 or later with Vulkan. Select your original MDK folder containing TRAVERSE, MISC, FALL3D and STREAM. To play in place, the app requires All files access and a writable folder. Progress stays in that folder. Choose Copy instead to avoid broad access. The app copies the game to Android/data/io.github.nemo22.mdk/files/mdk and keeps settings and saves in the parent files folder. Keep whichever location the app uses before uninstalling.

setup_notes.title: Keep your desktop files
setup_notes.instruction: For a Linux ARM64 copy you maintain, keep settings.cfg, saves, mods, captures and custom exports. Keep the whole MDK_USER_DIR if you set it, or the actual user-data fallback if the player folder is read-only. On first portable start, upstream can copy settings and saves from an older personal profile. Keep both copies until you know which one the player uses. Keep mdk_paths.cfg and your originals separately.

limitations: Optional HD texture generation downloads and starts a separate upscaling tool. Let it finish, or cancel and confirm it has stopped before updating, backing up or removing the player. You and upstream maintain the Linux ARM64 and Android copies.

entries.name: The Bigs 2 (The Bigs 2 ReXGlue)
entries.summary: Attach an independently permitted, prepared The Bigs 2 ReXGlue Windows player with your own Xbox 360 disc data already extracted upstream. Preserve its writable-package or existing per-user data layout; the published Windows package was only Wine-tested upstream.

setup.title: Prepare your own Xbox 360 game upstream
setup.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use, with your own supported The Bigs 2 Xbox 360 disc image. Complete the upstream first-launch extraction and settings outside Portcove, keep independent original media, and retain the exact accepted edition/revision. This reviewed route does not establish every region or patched image as compatible. No disc, helper, compiler or game is obtained or executed by this guide.

setup.title: Keep the complete official player
setup.instruction: The inspected v1.1 Windows ZIP contains TheBigs2-windows-x64/thebigs2.exe as an AMD64 native player with matching runtime libraries. It already contains the native game program; the first-launch UI extracts the original game data rather than compiling a new native player. Keep the complete package and notices. A development source build requiring Clang 20/ReXGlue is a separate route, not a prerequisite inferred for this existing player.

setup.title: Add the prepared player
setup.instruction: Select thebigs2.exe, use the complete extracted TheBigs2-windows-x64 directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the exact intent and request Play separately. The selected source configures paths, handles setup and resumes the linked game in process. If setup or disc extraction is still required, finish it outside the attached attempt. Quit the game normally; forced termination does not guarantee save flushing.

setup.title: Preserve the actual portable and external roots
setup.instruction: On Windows a writable executable folder enables upstream portable mode: preserve game/, config/thebigs2.toml, saves/ with profiles and achievements, cache/ and logs/. A non-writable folder instead uses the existing platform configuration path, normally %APPDATA%/thebigs2, and the runtime’s actual user-data/cache roots; preserve those independently rather than assuming all saves are in APPDATA. Existing command-line data/cache overrides and configuration take precedence. Upstream can copy old profiles into a new portable saves/ folder when it is absent; retain both originals and destinations. This guide performs no migration or deletion.

setup.title: Keep original and component permissions separate
setup.instruction: Retain the selected project’s Unlicense notice and its explicit exclusion of original/recompiled game code, the ReXGlue BSD-3-Clause notice and all other dependencies. Roboto and Barlow have separate Apache/OFL terms. No component grant licenses the original game or third-party mods; use only a complete copy you are independently permitted to use.

setup.title: Maintain the external copy and its limits
setup.instruction: Quit the actual game before upstream replacement, changing extraction/settings or restoring profiles. Keep independent recovery copies and review/relink changed executable bytes. Upstream explicitly reports the Windows package was cross-compiled and tested only through Wine; that does not establish physical Windows, full-game, save/reload or installed-app acceptance. Removing registration preserves external files; managed install/update/rollback/backup/removal and Supported status are not offered.

limitations: Preserve the active portable saves/configuration or external runtime paths. Wine-only upstream package testing is not Windows or complete-game qualification.

setup.title: Keep your saves, options and mods
setup.instruction: The Windows and Linux players store both options and saved progress in config beside the executable. Supported mods live in mods/ beside it. Keep both with their creating runtime and close the game normally before maintenance: the inspected title writes config during shutdown. Put replacement content in the supported mods tree; direct edits to shipped assets are outside the declared preserved data and can block update or removal until preserved and reconciled. setup.instruction: Install Tails Adventure by mechakotik from Google Play or choose the publisher’s Android APK on GitHub Releases. The inspected APK requires Android 5.0 or later and OpenGL ES 2.0. Keep using the same distribution channel for updates so your app signature stays compatible.

setup.title: Keep the Android save and mods
setup.instruction: With the game closed, preserve config and mods/ from the app’s writable files folder when your device gives you access, normally Android/data/com.mechakotik.tailsadventure/files. If the game cannot use external app storage, it saves config in private app storage. Check your Android backup before clearing app data, uninstalling or changing channels.

limitations: Upstream reports missing nonessential original features; completion/gameplay claims belong to upstream and have not been repeated here. Preserve a separate copy before changing mods or data.

entries.name: Medal of Honor: Allied Assault Breakthrough (OpenMoHAA)
entries.summary: Use the official OpenMoHAA player on Windows, Linux or Mac for Breakthrough with your own matching PC data. Keep original files and the external save profile backed up.
entries.game_title: Medal of Honor: Allied Assault Breakthrough

setup.title: Prepare the matching PC game
setup.instruction: Before Play, prepare your own complete Breakthrough PC data and its Allied Assault base game. Upstream recommends GOG Warchest; CD copies need the matching language patches (Allied Assault 1.11 and Breakthrough 2.40b). Keep the originals unchanged in a separate installation. Copy only the original PK3 files and sound/video resources into main, maintt beside the official player. Preserve the matching folder names and all required original resources; do not copy old executables, DLLs or unrelated expansion files over this runtime. Portcove does not verify original-game identity. Console editions and demos are different products. Keep the whole official runtime together. On Windows x64, install the upstream Visual C++ runtime if needed and use a short plain ASCII library path. Linux x64 needs glibc 2.34, libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.29 and system SDL2. The universal Mac package needs macOS 10.15 on Intel or macOS 11 on Apple Silicon.

setup.title: Keep an existing prepared copy
setup.instruction: Use a private working copy of the original game folder. Extract the complete official Windows x64 ZIP into it, preserving DLLs and companions. Follow upstream Visual C++ x64 runtime prerequisites when needed. Register launch_openmohaa_breakthrough.exe with the game root as working directory. This title-specific launcher selects Breakthrough and waits for openmohaa.exe to exit. Do not select omohaaded.exe, PDB archives or another expansion launcher. This remains a non-owning external registration. You and upstream own runtime replacement and every file; removing its registration preserves them. A catalog update does not migrate or adopt that copy.

setup_notes.title: Preserve your actual game data
setup_notes.instruction: Back up the game’s external profile separately. The normal locations are roaming application data on Windows, ~/.openmohaa on Linux and ~/Library/Application Support/openmohaa on Mac. When FLATPAK_ID is set and nonempty on Linux, the engine uses openmohaa under XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share. The Unix managed offer checks that the selected profile is outside the managed runtime and leaves it in place.

setup_notes.title: Set up the native Linux or Mac archive
setup_notes.instruction: For a separately prepared copy, extract the official Linux amd64 or arm64 ZIP or the universal Mac ZIP. Keep the executables and libraries together. If the extracted launcher and engine have no execute permission, make those two files executable with chmod u+x launch_openmohaa_breakthrough openmohaa. From that folder, run ./launch_openmohaa_breakthrough with your own patched PC data in main, maintt.

setup_notes.title: Use the Windows ARM64 package
setup_notes.instruction: On Windows ARM64, choose the official ARM64 ZIP. After preparing the same original files, use launch_openmohaa_breakthrough.exe in the extracted folder. You and upstream own that copy and its profile.

limitations: Back up the actual external profile and your originals separately before changing runtimes.
A separately prepared copy can use a custom profile or fall back to its runtime when the engine cannot find a home directory. Preserve the actual profile with its creating runtime.

setup.title: Set up Yakumo on Linux, Steam Deck, Mac or Android
setup.instruction: On x64 Linux or Steam Deck, open the Flatpak through your desktop or Steam; it uses the Freedesktop Platform 25.08 runtime. If you unpack the x64 tarball instead, start it with ./yakumo from the unpacked folder so the launcher sets the stack size; it needs glibc 2.29 or later, a Vulkan driver and the Vulkan loader. The publisher uses ad hoc signing; follow its macOS guide for the first-open prompt. On Android 10 or later with Vulkan 1.1, install the ARM64 APK and choose your ISO in the Android file picker. setup.instruction: Select Yakumo.exe and use its containing folder as the working directory. Leave arguments empty. Keep the complete independently permitted runtime and finish the title-specific preparation before Play.

setup_notes.instruction: Keep settings.ini, prepared EBOOT.ELF, copied disc.iso or its external in-place original, ms0/PSP/SAVEDATA (including ULJM05800, ULJM05800QST and ULJM05800DAT), mods, texture packs, pipeline caches/keys, logs, controller mappings, translations/fonts, save-backups, temporary files and all custom roots. The Flatpak keeps data in ~/.var/app/io.github.teamgdb.Yakumo/data/Yakumo/MHP3rd and can export saves to Downloads. The Linux tarball uses $XDG_DATA_HOME/Yakumo/MHP3rd or ~/.local/share/Yakumo/MHP3rd by default. The Mac app uses ~/Library/Application Support/Yakumo/MHP3rd. Keep your actual profile and any ISO used in place before replacing the app. Yakumo checks NPJB-40001 and encrypted EBOOT.BIN SHA-256 79e25f3512d56e0f7bf5c48351d7d0d255269675ffc8811ac5599322bb66945e, then verifies prepared EBOOT.ELF SHA-256 55c0598436c0753b04331f8e95d406f832d9217806e3a896fed0e88b33637d8c. The check covers those files and the disc ID.

setup_notes.instruction: Portcove records the selected executable, working folder and literal arguments after review. Play is separate and only the selected process is supervised. Managed installation, backup, rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for this external copy.

setup_notes.instruction: You and upstream own the external copy's data: the data folder the copy actually uses, chosen in this order: a --data-dir folder, the MHP3RD_DATA_DIR folder, data beside Yakumo.exe when portable.txt or a data folder is there (unless MHP3RD_PORTABLE=0), then %APPDATA%\Yakumo\MHP3rd; plus any game folder it starts with and any disc image used in place. setup_notes.instruction: Portcove installs and replaces its separate official runtime using the declared release rules. Existing external registrations retain their files and user/upstream ownership. limitations: MIT covers the project’s own original code; third-party IP remains independently owned. Preserve the applicable packaged FFmpeg LGPL and font/dependency notices; this is not a whole-game rights certificate.

Upstream documents untranslated/blank save-dialog screens, curved-surface issues and unsupported code mods; reported rendering, multiplayer, controller and save compatibility are publisher claims, not Portcove observations. No game, original, helper, installer or native session was run.

For a copy you prepared yourself, the Windows installed profile normally uses %APPDATA%/Yakumo/MHP3rd and the upstream ZIP with portable.txt uses data/ beside the executable. A non-writable data directory fails instead of silently falling back.

entries.summary: Register a permitted noncommercial completed Yoshi Windows cycle player, preserving your original, actual configuration and creating-backend state.

setup.title: Prepare a permitted completed cycle player
setup.instruction: Use an already permitted noncommercial source-built Yoshi Windows cycle player under the selected title/framework PolyForm Noncommercial terms and applicable component notices; the shared UI has separate MIT terms. Complete upstream generation/build outside Portcove in a separate folder. This handoff is not a package/component attestation, does not grant original-game or optional media rights, and does not establish a legacy or HD executable as the cycle product.

setup.title: Keep the supported original and backend together
setup.instruction: Use your own current supported USA Yoshi payload: CRC32 E7EAD93B, 128 KiB PRG plus 32 KiB CHR. The documented canonical NES 2.0 file SHA-1 is 71cc02d4a005c6ad71f1fbf2b3ccd890d65056a3. Upstream accepts the older header declaring 64 KiB CHR only for the complete known payload and length; this is not acceptance of arbitrary truncation, revisions or regions. The previous larger input and its states are a separate unqualified contract.

setup.title: Select the completed native player and actual configuration
setup.instruction: Select the already working completed cycle YoshiRecomp.exe, using its containing runtime folder as working directory for normal defaults. Preserve an already working custom working directory and the interpretation of existing path arguments instead of changing them merely to register. Do not choose setup.bat, setup.sh, a compiler, headless tool or another backend executable. Use one literal argument token: the absolute path to your supported ROM, with spaces kept inside that token. The ordinary upstream launcher remains available; these cycle builds do not accept the SNES --rom or --no-launcher flags. Preserve an established --config and its absolute path as separate tokens when already used; do not switch configuration merely to register.

setup.title: Review launch details, then choose Play
setup.instruction: Review and consent to the exact native executable, working directory and literal arguments. Registration does not compile, migrate, repair or launch the game. Choose Play separately; upstream’s ordinary launcher and game loop are in-process in the selected source. Portcove observes the selected process, not an exclusive process family. Relink an upstream replacement through a new review and close every actual player before upstream changes.

setup.title: Keep your working copy and use the project’s updates
setup.instruction: Preserve the whole creating runtime/source tree, original, config.ini and any custom configuration, its rom.cfg, older keybinds.ini, mods, cycle states under saves/<ROM stem>.cycstate, diagnostics/captures and all custom paths. Yoshi has no battery-backed save, but that does not make its cycle states disposable. Legacy binary states and states from the previous larger ROM are not qualified for this cycle/input; keep each with its creating copy. Do not rename or import old files merely to register. Upstream/player own preparation, repair and runtime replacement. Removing registration removes only Portcove metadata and preserves all external bytes.

limitations: Default settings use executable-parent config.ini; rom.cfg follows the chosen settings file. A custom --config is not an all-writes redirect: default cartridge battery/state paths remain executable-relative. Preserve actual existing --save-file choices; do not add --save-file or --no-save merely to register. --no-save disables battery loading as well as writing.

These upstream previews and their source/backend migration reports are not Portcove gameplay or save-compatibility qualification. Core user-selected registration does not authenticate the ROM, generated code, component rights or build provenance. setup.instruction: Use a complete copy and components you are independently permitted to use, with your own stock GoldenEye007 USA N64 cartridge image. The reviewed 1.0.2b instructions accept .z64 big-endian, .v64 byte-swapped and .n64 word-swapped inputs; names/extensions are not identity checks. The expected stock size is12,582,912bytes; source normalizes byte order and checks header CRCs DCBC50D1/09FD1AA3 and full normalized CRC32 B6330846. These checks are not cryptographic authenticity or entitlement proof. Follow upstream preparation outside Portcove, retaining the original image. This is not the Xbox360 XBLA edition or another GoldenEye port.

setup.instruction: After upstream setup has the intended ROM in Data or its already configured location, select ProjectMidas.exe, use its complete extracted package directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. setup.instruction: Quit the actual game normally before upstream repair or replacement; retain independent copies and review/relink changed executable bytes. Linux blank-triangle limitations and upstream co-op/netplay/mod work remain at their own scope. No Portcove gameplay, multiplayer, save/reload, native-installed or Supported acceptance is claimed. entries.name: One Must Fall 2097 / OpenOMF (omf2097)
entries.summary: Explore One Must Fall 2097 / OpenOMF (omf2097) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

setup.title: Start the managed Windows player
setup.instruction: The official archive includes the freeware One Must Fall 2097 resources and the native OpenOMF player. Choose Play after installation; no commercial source files or generation step are needed. The package also includes an ARM64 player; this route uses openomf.exe for x86-64.

setup.title: Start the managed Linux AppImage
setup.instruction: Install the stable x86-64 AppImage in Portcove and choose Play. Your Linux system needs AppImage support. The package includes the freeware resources and SDL2. The v0.8.6 AppImage also needs your system’s libjack.so.0 and libpipewire-0.3.so.0. Use your distribution’s packages if Play reports either library missing. For a custom OpenOMF override or alternate resource set, keep a separately prepared copy.

setup.title: Prepare the upstream Apple Silicon package
setup.instruction: Extract the stable Apple Silicon ZIP into a separate folder. If it contains usr/bin/openomf, check the Homebrew library requirements below and keep the entire usr tree. Set OPENOMF_RESOURCE_PATH to the absolute path to the extracted usr/share/games/openomf folder when launching that player. If the package instead contains OpenOMF.app, keep the app intact and follow its release instructions.

setup_notes.title: Check the inspected stable packages
setup_notes.instruction: The inspected 0.8.6 AppImage needs glibc 2.38 or later for its bundled libraries. The separate 0.8.6 Linux TAR.GZ needs glibc 2.43 and system libraries. The loose 0.8.6 Apple Silicon ZIP needs macOS 14 and Homebrew libepoxy, confuse, enet, sdl2_mixer, libxmp, libpng, opusfile, miniupnpc, libnatpmp and sdl2-compat. The binary loads specific library versions from /opt/homebrew. The macOS 15 app layout was observed on the separate rolling channel.

setup_notes.title: Find the effective OpenOMF profile
setup_notes.instruction: After explicit OpenOMF overrides, upstream checks XDG_CONFIG_HOME for configuration and XDG_STATE_HOME for state, then the SDL preference directory. Preserve settings, saves, scores, recordings, screenshots and user mods at their effective locations.

limitations: Portcove manages the selected Windows and Linux runtime packages. You and upstream maintain independently prepared copies, including the Mac package. Back up the actual configuration and state folders separately. An explicit OPENOMF_CONFIG_PATH or OPENOMF_STATE_PATH can change those locations.

entries.name: Open Nectar (Pikmin)
entries.summary: Native Pikmin port from Open Nectar; gameplay has not been tested by Portcove.

setup.title: Windows x64 separate upstream copy
setup.instruction: If you already have a permitted Open Nectar 1.3 or 1.1.1 Windows x64 copy, run nectar-launcher.exe from a separate folder outside the Portcove library. Choose Install under Pikmin, provide your own supported USA Rev. 1 or Europe disc and choose a separate writable destination. Keep verification enabled. Preserve the installation and its active config folder or LOCALAPPDATA/Open Nectar.

setup.title: Linux x64 upstream launcher
setup.instruction: For a permitted 1.3 or 1.1.1 Linux x64 copy, extract nectar-linux.tar.gz and open nectar-launcher, or make Open_Nectar-x86_64.AppImage executable and open it. The 1.3 package needs glibc 2.30 or newer. Use OpenGL 3.3 and zenity or kdialog for the file picker. Choose Install under Pikmin, select your own USA Rev. 1 or Europe ISO or GCM and a separate writable folder. The launcher can use Dolphin Tool for RVZ, WIA and GCZ. Keep disc verification enabled. After setup, use the launcher in the selected installation for Play and updates.

setup.title: Android ARM64 upstream launcher
setup.instruction: For an already permitted 1.1.1 Android ARM64 copy on Android 11 or later, allow All files access for its chosen data folder. Use Install under Pikmin with your own matching ISO or GCM. The default folder is OpenNectar in shared storage. Pikmin 2 uses its own disc and setup.

setup.title: Android ARM64 1.2 and 1.3 data folder
setup.instruction: For an already permitted 1.2 or 1.3 copy, use Android 10 or newer and OpenGL ES 3.0. On Android 10 grant the storage permission. On Android 11 or newer use Allow access to all files. Choose a writable folder in shared storage outside the Android folder. The default is OpenNectar in shared storage. Choose Install under Pikmin and select your own matching ISO or GCM in the system picker. Preserve your selected folder and export the memory cards before updating.

setup.title: Set up a separate Apple Silicon copy
setup.instruction: For a permitted Open Nectar 1.3 copy, extract nectar-macos.tar.gz on Apple Silicon with macOS 11 or newer. Follow the bundled README.txt for first launch, then open nectar-launcher. Choose Install under Pikmin and supply your own matching USA Rev. 1 or Europe disc and a writable installation folder. Use the launcher in that installation for later Play and updates.

setup.title: Build a separate Intel Mac copy
setup.instruction: With an already permitted 1.2 source checkout, use Xcode Command Line Tools, CMake and a Mac with OpenGL 4.1. Follow scripts/build-macos.sh. It builds both Pikmin regions and also builds a separate Pikmin 2 player. Start build/pikmin1/bin/nectar-launcher, choose Install under Pikmin and select your matching disc and a writable destination.

setup.title: Keep the creating installation and data
setup.instruction: Close the game and launcher before copying their data. On Linux preserve the installed folder, including saves, and the active settings location, either its config directory or open-nectar under XDG_CONFIG_HOME (usually ~/.config). On Android retain the actual chosen data folder and use the upstream export for memory cards. The card ZIP covers the cards only. After Pikmin setup completes on a supported desktop, choose Use an existing installation. Select the prepared copy's native nectar-launcher.exe on Windows or nectar-launcher on Linux or Mac and its containing folder. Use that launcher's Pikmin Play control. The launcher owns game preparation and updates. Use the Android launcher directly on Android. Removing the registration leaves the external files in place.

setup_notes.title: Keep the Mac and Android data you actually use
setup_notes.instruction: On Mac keep the selected installation, its saves and the active settings folder. The launcher defaults to pikmin-native under XDG_DATA_HOME, or ~/.local/share/pikmin-native. On Android preserve the actual chosen OpenNectar folder and export the memory cards before replacing the copy. The card export covers only the cards.

limitations: Use only a copy and bundled components you are already permitted to use. The upstream CC0 notice excludes Nintendo and other third-party material, and the package includes a separate Pikmin 2 runtime. An attributable grant for that bundled game code or a separately qualified package is needed before fresh acquisition can be offered.
Keep the player-managed folder outside Portcove's managed installation. Preserve the creating installation and profile. The existing managed Windows acquisition hold remains in place.
original_requirements: Pikmin USA Rev. 1 or Europe disc; Open Nectar checks it during preparation.

setup_notes.instruction: The separately maintained PlayFDroid OpenArena Android release has touchscreen controls and downloads the official game data into app-specific storage on first launch. Follow its release and installation instructions. Desktop profile folders do not apply to that app.

setup.title: Install OpenClonk
setup.instruction: On Windows x64, use the Windows 64-bit installer. On Linux, use your distribution’s openclonk package or the community OpenClonk Flatpak for x86-64. Debian also packages OpenClonk for ARM64. The publisher’s Linux archives were built with Ubuntu 16.04, so try your distribution’s package first on a newer system.

setup.title: Choose a player and scenario
setup.instruction: Create a player, or select an existing one under Player Selection and choose Activate. Open Start Game, open Tutorials, and start Wandering Wipf to learn the controls. The packages include the game data.

setup_notes.title: Find your player data
setup_notes.instruction: On Windows, look under %APPDATA%\OpenClonk. Windows stores default settings in HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\OpenClonk Project\OpenClonk. Keep that key if you want to transfer these settings. On Linux, keep ~/.clonk/openclonk, including its config file. The Flatpak profile is ~/.var/app/org.openclonk.OpenClonk/.clonk/openclonk.

limitations: Close OpenClonk before copying players, scenarios, or saves. Keep any custom user data directory or separate configuration file you selected.

entries.name: Halo: Combat Evolved / OpenCE (OpenCommunityEdition)
entries.summary: Play Halo: Combat Evolved through OpenCE with your own Xbox disc image.

setup.title: Choose your original Xbox disc image on first Play
setup.instruction: On first Play, select your own Halo: Combat Evolved Xbox .iso or .xiso; every edition works. OpenCE extracts its maps into the maps folder beside the player. Keep the disc image outside the game folder, because the game offers any image it finds there. Halo PC or Custom Edition maps do not replace these Xbox maps.

setup.title: Run a Windows copy you manage yourself
setup.instruction: Extract halo-windows-release.zip into its own folder and start halo.exe with no arguments. Use the release package for playing. Debug builds stop at failed assertions, and symbol archives contain debug information. OpenCE asks before installing its own updates and can replace its program files when you accept.

setup.title: Run the external Linux player
setup.instruction: Extract halo-linux-release.zip and keep libSDL3.so.0 beside halo. Make halo executable if needed with chmod u+x halo and run ./halo from that folder. Use a Linux host that can run 32-bit x86 programs. It needs 32-bit glibc 2.29 or newer, OpenGL and display libraries, and PipeWire or PulseAudio client libraries. Choose your own Xbox ISO or XISO on first launch. The file picker needs a desktop portal or zenity. If neither is available, start with a copy of the image beside halo. OpenCE handles updates for this external copy.

setup_notes.title: Keep all actual data locations
setup_notes.instruction: Beside the program OpenCE keeps config.toml, the extracted maps, custom_maps, mods, load_order.toml, screenshots, crash reports and debug logs. The default profile, save and shader cache location is AppData/Roaming/halo on Windows and $XDG_DATA_HOME/halo-linux on Linux, usually ~/.local/share/halo-linux. If paths.saves or HALO_SAVE_ROOT overrides it, copy the configured location before an update.

setup_notes.title: Use the publisher’s Android release
setup_notes.instruction: On a 64-bit ARM device with Android 9 or newer, extract app-release.apk from halo-android-release.zip and install it with Android’s package installer. Start OpenCE and choose your own Halo Xbox ISO or XISO with the system picker. Allow about 2 GB for the extracted maps. The app handles its own updates. Before uninstalling, copy your maps and the save/u profiles from Android/data/com.halo.decomp/files. That app folder also contains config.toml and mods.

limitations: OpenCE is a port of a Halo: Combat Evolved decompilation; the project’s AGPL licence does not cover the original game code. Portcove downloads it only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files.
Optional Halo Custom Edition maps and their matching resources belong in custom_maps. OpenSauce maps are incompatible.

Clicking a Halo or Discord invite starts OpenCE directly, outside Portcove, using the version that last registered the link. Close any game started that way before updating or rolling back in Portcove, and start OpenCE from Portcove once after an update before using an invite.

setup.title: Complete original-game setup in OpenJKDF2
setup.instruction: Extract the complete Windows player package and choose openjkdf2-64.exe with its containing folder as the working directory. Soundtrack disc extraction is separate; the player does not supply original game data. The published player is a debug build and includes an upstream runtime updater.

setup.title: Save launch details before Play
setup.instruction: Save launch details in Portcove, then choose Play separately. Registration does not adopt the files or grant managed Backup, Rollback or removal of the external folder.

setup.title: Add the game and manage your files
setup.instruction: Register the real Windows player with its matching working directory and separate literal arguments; do not select a converter, installer or updater as the game player. Complete any original-data or prerequisite setup deliberately through upstream instructions. Registration does not perform or authenticate that preparation, and Play is a separate explicit action.

setup.title: Prepare the Apple Silicon build
setup.instruction: Unpack the official v0.9.9 macos-debug.tar.gz using Mac archive tools and open OpenJKDF2_universal.app on Apple Silicon with macOS 12 or newer. Choose your own complete Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II installation in its setup flow. Keep the Resource and Episode folders from the same game edition.

setup.title: Prepare the upstream Android build
setup.instruction: Install the official v0.9.9 ARM64 Android APK on an OpenGL ES 3 device. In Android Files, open the OpenJKDF2 files and put your own Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II game folders inside jk1/. Keep the Resource and Episode folders together. Preserve your jk1/ profile before app removal and use a same-signed upstream APK for in-place replacement.

setup_notes.title: Build and run upstream on Linux
setup_notes.instruction: For Linux x86-64 or ARM64, follow the 64-bit Linux/SDL2 section of the v0.9.9 build guide at https://github.com/shinyquagsire23/OpenJKDF2/blob/v0.9.9/BUILDING.md. Check out tag v0.9.9 before initializing the submodules. Use the guide’s Clang setup and launch the built player from the checkout as documented so it can find its libraries. Copy the Resource and Episode folders from your own matching Jedi Knight installation into the working folder as lowercase resource/ and episode/. Linux filenames can be case-sensitive. Keep the working copy and actual profile when rebuilding. You build, launch and update this Linux copy through upstream.

setup_notes.title: Preserve imported Jedi Knight data and profiles
setup_notes.instruction: Before changing versions, preserve the actual imported game-data folder and player profiles/saves, resource, episode, MUSIC, expansions and custom mods, plus local cvars/binds/registry JSON, screenshots and any selected custom paths.
