entries.name: Perimeter: Emperor's Testament (Perimeter community engine)
entries.summary: Prepare Perimeter: Emperor's Testament through its upstream player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.

setup.title: Use the matching original game
setup.instruction: Use your own complete Perimeter: Emperor’s Testament resources (models, textures, sounds, text, Resource and Scripts). The other title does not automatically supply this game. Exact retail patch/localization and shared-base requirements remain unpinned; preserve the complete matching original installation.

setup.title: Prepare the Windows player
setup.instruction: The inspected 3.0.10 GitHub release inventory has no binary assets. Follow upstream INSTALL.eng.md to build the Windows player and its required DLLs, or use an already prepared working upstream player. Keep a private working game copy. Register perimeter.exe and retain its working directory. The upstream content override is one literal argument, content= followed by the absolute folder containing Resource and Scripts. Do not infer that the linked Legate Edition retail distribution includes both classic campaigns.

setup.title: Prepare the Linux player
setup.instruction: On a 64-bit Linux system with glibc 2.28 or later, use Perimeter Release x86_64 from a successful main-branch push on the official Linux Build workflow at https://github.com/KD-lab-Open-Source/Perimeter/actions/workflows/linux_build.yml. Unzip the download and unpack Perimeter.tar. Keep the perimeter executable beside libdxvk_d3d9.so and libsteam_api.so. Use the system SDL2, SDL2_image, SDL2_mixer and SDL2_net libraries and a working Vulkan graphics driver. If a build is unavailable, follow the upstream Linux build guide. Select the native perimeter file and its containing folder. For Perimeter: Emperor's Testament, add content= followed by the absolute path of your private copy as one argument line. The folder must contain Perimeter.ini, Resource and Scripts. Keep any spaces inside that one argument.

setup.title: Add the game and manage your files
setup.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Select the game executable and its working folder, and put each launch argument on a separate line. Choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, originals, saves and settings. Removing its registration leaves those external files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Close the game and keep a working copy and every data and profile folder before changing versions.

setup_notes.title: Keep your existing game data
setup_notes.instruction: Preserve the complete working game folder, actual upstream configuration/profile and any explicitly selected content or save locations. The reviewed documentation and source do not establish one universal Windows persistence coordinate; registration does not convert saves, adopt data or prove another campaign compatible.

limitations: No downloadable Windows package was found in the inspected GitHub releases. Windows CPU architecture depends on the actual prepared build; a managed package route remains pending a concrete artifact and preparation/maintenance fit.
Use a prepared x86-64 player and a private copy of the matching game. If a GOG installer puts Perimeter.ini in _support, copy it to the root of your prepared copy.

entries.name: Planescape: Torment (original) (GemRB)
entries.summary: Set up Planescape: Torment (original) through its upstream gemrb player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.

setup.title: Use this original game and edition
setup.instruction: Use a complete installed original Planescape: Torment working copy. Enhanced Edition and the included trivial demo do not supply this target. Preserve the chosen language and patches with that working copy. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files.

setup.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
setup.instruction: For Windows x64, use the official SourceForge archive with its plugins, scripts and configuration. Its v0.9.5 ZIP is named gemrb-win32-v0.9.5.zip and contains a 64-bit player. The player needs the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime. Give this game its own configuration: GamePath points to a separate complete working copy of the installed original; GameType=pst. Use the configuration supplied with your actual build rather than leaving @...@ development-template placeholders. Register gemrb.exe with the complete GemRB installation as working directory and two literal argument lines, -c then the absolute path to this game’s configuration.

setup.title: Keep your originals and game data
setup.instruction: Choose a dedicated empty private CachePath for this game: GemRB clears that directory, so it must never be your originals, saves or profile root. SavePath is the parent containing save/, not save/ itself. Keep a separate SavePath per game.

setup.title: Choose the upstream Linux build
setup.instruction: Use the official x86-64 GemRB AppImage with the host libjack.so.0 library, or install org.gemrb.gemrb from Flathub on x86-64 or ARM64 Linux. Start the Flatpak normally once to create GemRB.cfg in ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/config/gemrb. For that package, copy this title’s complete original working copy to ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/data/planescape-torment, and use that absolute GamePath in a separate planescape-torment.cfg. Use a writable SavePath parent and an empty, dedicated CachePath under the same app’s data and cache directories. Start with flatpak run --command=gemrb org.gemrb.gemrb -c followed by the absolute config path in quotes. This passes the path to the player as one argument. setup.instruction: Use your own DOS PowerSlave or Exhumed data folder, anchored by STUFF.DAT. Raze recognizes the distinct supported PowerSlave and Exhumed data identities. Keep the complete accompanying original data. The Saturn/PlayStation games and the 2022 Exhumed remaster are different implementations/data contracts. Raze searches installed Steam/GOG copies and configured game-data folders. Reuse a recognized copy; do not duplicate it unnecessarily. If it is not found, add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini, or in raze_portable.ini for the Portcove-managed Windows player; do not copy game files into the managed player folder, because Portcove verifies that folder. Elsewhere, you may instead place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

setup.title: Choose Play in the upstream player
setup.instruction: On Windows, choose Install, then Play explicitly. Portcove downloads and verifies the official Windows ZIP, keeps the player folder together, and creates Raze’s portable configuration marker so its configuration, saves, screenshots and demos stay beside the managed player, where Portcove preserves them across updates. Raze may ask which detected game/edition to use, because the same player supports several games. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your STUFF.DAT archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

setup.title: Keep upstream update ownership and platform handoffs
setup.instruction: On Windows, Portcove replaces the managed runtime and preserves its declared data. A separate existing Windows copy stays yours: registering it preserves every external file and Portcove does not manage its Update, Backup or Rollback, and the normal-profile settings described below are not imported into a managed install. Elsewhere, you and upstream replace this external player. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. A native Linux build outside Flatpak uses its own profile, usually ~/.config/raze. Preserve that profile and any older ~/.raze directory before launching a replacement.

setup.title: Use Raze from Flathub on Linux
setup.instruction: Install org.zdoom.Raze from Flathub for Linux x64 or ARM64. Make sure ~/.config exists in your home directory. Keep your original files and place a complete working copy of this game's data in its own subfolder under ~/.var/app/org.zdoom.Raze/.config/raze. Open Raze and choose this game if a picker appears. Close Raze and back up its actual configuration, saves and mods before updating through Flatpak.

setup_notes.title: Keep the shared profile this game uses
setup_notes.instruction: A Portcove-managed Windows install keeps raze_portable.ini, Save, Screenshots and Demos beside the managed player and does not share or import the normal-profile locations described next. Windows normally keeps raze.ini in Documents/My Games/raze, saves under the system Saved Games/Raze folder, and screenshots in the system Screenshots/Raze folder; redirected Windows known folders can change those absolute locations. A writable raze_portable.ini outside Program Files uses the player folder with Save and Screenshots instead. Custom -config/-savedir locations remain external. Normal save roots contain game/edition subfolders. A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.

limitations: A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.

entries.name: Ace Combat 04: Shattered Skies (Ace Combat 04: Shattered Skies - PC Port)
entries.summary: A work-in-progress Ace Combat 04 beta, rather than a complete remaster or confirmed campaign. The Windows installer and separate source route translate the PS2 main CPU and build locally from your own USA SLUS-20152 executable and disc data; hardware/runtime services remain separate responsibilities. Exact host CPU architecture follows the selected setup guide, while accepted revision/hashes and BIOS/firmware needs are unconfirmed here. You and the project manage installation and replacement. Portcove has not qualified the installer or confirmed setup or gameplay.

setup.title: Finish the official Windows preparation
setup.instruction: Use the official v2.2.3-beta setup with your own unmodified Ace Combat 04: Shattered Skies USA PS2 ISO, SLUS-20152. The selected original executable SLUS_201.52 must be 3248756 bytes with SHA256 38ecebd6965c2f74ec8973f538781506bf3a2cfad86f908deb6c5d585d528301; this is not a whole-ISO hash. Complete setup into an empty chosen folder and retain your original independently. The release setup carries the runtime and needs .NET Framework 4.8, about 4 GB free and Vulkan 1.3; the separate developer source-build route is not required merely to install this package.

setup.title: Keep the locally assembled game unit
setup.instruction: Retain the complete prepared folder: Ace Combat 04.exe, runtime/ac4.exe and its DLLs, shaders, generated local memory image, original disc data, settings and notices. The installer verifies the original executable and creates the memory image from the user’s disc; the download is not a ready-to-run substitute for that disc. Do not confuse the installer, runtime, graphics replay developer tool or another Ace Combat title.

setup.title: Attach the waiting game launcher
setup.instruction: Select Ace Combat 04.exe in the prepared game folder, use that folder as working directory and pass the exact existing supported ISO or extracted disc directory as the first argument. Review the selected program, working folder and arguments and choose Play when ready. This avoids the launcher’s fallback of picking the first alphabetically sorted ISO when several are present. The selected launcher supplies runtime data, shader/save context and normal unbounded-play options to runtime/ac4.exe and waits for it to exit, draining its logs. Keep both processes in the ordinary session and close the game normally; do not select DIAGNOSTICS.bat or the setup program as Play.

setup.title: Preserve this runtime’s card format and paths
setup.instruction: Keep the whole writable prepared root, saves/, runtime/ac4_settings.ini, runtime/ac4_pipelines.* where actually created, last-play.log, textures/mods, original disc and recovery copies. The launcher clears inherited PS2_* overrides and explicitly sets its own runtime/shaders and root/saves; a bare runtime launched in another context can select different paths. Its card format is this runtime’s, not PCSX2’s. Do not merge, convert or overwrite populated cards. Upstream updates use a new game folder; retain the old one and verify the intended save copy separately. No card copy, migration, restore or deletion is performed here.

setup.title: Keep beta and upstream ownership boundaries
setup.instruction: The game’s main CPU functions are compiled to native code; the runtime separately implements console services, graphics/vector units, audio, movies, cards and input. Retain project and component notices; original assets and optional user-made texture packs are separate. Published setup and upstream reports do not establish a complete campaign, remaster, physical controller or real-save reload on this host. Quit normally before upstream replacement, retain recovery and review/relink changed bytes. No native/installed, Supported or managed install/update/rollback/backup/deletion acceptance is asserted.

limitations: Select the prepared Ace Combat 04.exe with the exact own disc path. Keep runtime/ and the runtime-specific saves together; do not use PCSX2 cards or infer full campaign acceptance from this beta.

setup.instruction: Extract the complete Windows x64 ZIP into a writable folder. Use Windows 10 or 11 with Vulkan support. Install the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015–2022 Redistributable (x64) if needed. Open WinBackRecompiled.exe and select your own big-endian WinBack USA .z64 (SHA-1 fa04477b321a95e1f7a2edcac5c09bfa6ef72041). The game verifies and keeps a copy in its folder.

setup.title: Select the prepared player
setup.instruction: Select WinBackRecompiled.exe and use its containing folder as the working directory. Leave arguments empty. Keep the complete independently permitted runtime and finish the title-specific preparation before Play.

setup_notes.title: Setup instructions for the inspected release
setup_notes.instruction: https://github.com/RetroPulse03/WinBackRecomp/releases/tag/v0.2.0

setup_notes.title: Registration ownership and removal
setup_notes.instruction: Portcove records the selected executable, working folder and literal arguments after review. Play is separate and only the selected process is supervised. You and upstream own replacement and updates; relink changed executable bytes after reviewing them. Removing this registration preserves every external file. Managed installation, backup, rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for this external copy.

setup_notes.title: Player-data ownership
setup_notes.instruction: You and upstream own the external copy's data: ROM copy, settings.json, saves/ including Controller Pak and checkpoints, mods and renderer data in the game folder. Back up these locations separately; registration does not migrate or certify their compatibility.

limitations: Save through the game before quitting. The BASIC level-select option does not restore previously recorded checkpoint progress. The project reports limited testing beyond the first mission.
The project reports that this release can crash on exit.

setup.instruction: Keep the entire saves/ folder beside the executable, the existing ROM location, config.ini and any user assets/settings. Upstream F8 saving replaces that ROM’s previous state slot; F9 loading replaces current progress. Execution states are not a promise of cartridge-battery format or compatibility between releases. Do not overwrite a saved state, merge another title’s data or reset settings to add the reference. Portcove performs no save conversion, import, migration, backup or restore.

setup.instruction: Finish upstream single-player setup with your own supported RTCW Main data, including pak0.pk3 and applicable sp_pak1/sp_pak2/sp_pak3 and patch-data-141/locale files. setup.instruction: Use the actual prepared working directory and same supported literal arguments. Preserve established fs_basepath/fs_homepath/fs_game choices and absolute custom roots as actually configured. Review exact intent/consent, then choose Play separately. Do not override the host profile root or force an unrelated empty profile to attach the player.

setup.title: Preserve complete external state
setup.instruction: Default Windows home data follows the actual Documents/RTCW known-folder location; configured roots and Main/game subdirectories may differ. Preserve the whole runtime and original data plus actual configs/profiles/saves/screenshots/demos/mods/unknown files in every base/home/game/custom/legacy root. Keep the old creating tuple before any upstream replacement. GPL engine and additional SP/component terms do not license the original game; no multiplayer, mod, or cross-version save compatibility follows from this registration.

setup.title: Update the game and remove its registration
setup.instruction: Close every running copy before changing external files. You manage setup, game replacement, profile changes, data migration and recovery. Keep the working game version and every data folder, update it with the project’s tools, then review and select the changed executable before choosing Play. Portcove monitors only the process you selected and agreed to launch. It does not prevent other copies from running, restrict file access or take over unrelated helpers or replacement processes. Removing the registration leaves external files in place. This route does not offer Portcove downloads, setup, updates, backups, rollback, data migration or deletion.

limitations: Use only a copy and content you are already permitted to use. These instructions do not establish permission for the original game or other components, or confirm the resulting game files.
These instructions do not confirm gameplay, saving, mods, network play, physical controls or behavior on other platforms.

setup.instruction: On Linux x64, choose the AppImage, Flatpak bundle or tar.gz. The tar.gz clients require glibc 2.38 or later, SDL2, zlib, Opus, Opusfile and Vorbisfile. The two desktop tar.gz archives need executable permission on the client files after extraction.

setup.title: Supply the original game data
setup.instruction: For an owned Steam installation the upstream engine can search standard Steam paths. For a manual desktop archive setup, copy the original files into main beside the extracted clients. For the AppImage, you can set an accessible game data root with +set fs_basepath and put main under that root. Single-player needs pak0.pk3 and sp_pak1.pk3 through sp_pak3.pk3. Follow the upstream list for the multiplayer packs. Leave the original game installation intact.

setup.title: Choose the client and preserve your profile
setup.instruction: Run iowolfsp for the campaign or iowolfmp for multiplayer using the executable for your computer. The Linux AppImage and Flatpak launch single-player unless --mp is the first argument. The iowolfded executable is the dedicated server. Before replacing the engine, back up the active fs_homepath and retain any custom fs_basepath and fs_game settings.

limitations: The Apple Silicon archive requires macOS 15 or later and loads sdl2, opusfile, opus, libvorbis, libogg, jpeg-turbo, and freetype from /opt/homebrew. The publisher supplies no Intel Mac, Linux ARM64, or Android package in this release.
The Windows x64 clients need a compatible zlib1.dll, which is missing from the publisher's 1.0.0 ZIP.

entries.summary: Attach an independently permitted, prepared Fukami Windows application with your supported Ridge Racer V disc. Its native parent prepares and waits for a same-image game child; preserve actual LocalAppData, memory cards, extracted-disc data and matching resource packages.

setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Ridge Racer V USA SLUS-20002 as CHD or a complete CUE/BIN pair. This is a per-file source contract, not a hash of every disc representation. Complete upstream disc selection/extraction and settings first; keep the original independently. setup.instruction: The inspected official 1.1.0 Windows x86-64 ZIP contains AMD64 Fukami/Fukami.exe and its matching libraries, resources/ package and share/fukami-default.ini/workload contract. Keep that full layout. It differs from a developer runtime, an extracted ELF or the macOS/Linux products. setup.title: Add the prepared app that waits for the game
setup.instruction: Select Fukami.exe, use its complete extracted Fukami folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the exact intent and request Play separately. Source creates a same-image child with the configured environment and original ELF, waits without a play-session timer and returns its exit status; it can restart that child after an upstream settings restart. Keep that supported parent rather than inventing environment/child flags or attaching a resource DLL. Finish missing-disc preparation outside the attached attempt. The source attempts a kill-on-close job on a best-effort basis; this is not an observed universal descendant-cleanup or save-flush guarantee.

setup.title: Preserve actual cards and resource/data roots
setup.instruction: Normally keep %LOCALAPPDATA%/Fukami with fukami.ini, mc/ memory cards, disc/ extracted originals, sessions/ when logging is enabled and all other player data. The real Windows known folder can be relocated; an established FUKAMI_DATA_DIR selects another per-run root. Keep the source CHD or complete CUE/BIN and any external texture/settings/card paths, plus the matching immutable resource package. Card persistence, state files and session logs are distinct. This guide changes no environment and performs no extraction, migration, backup, restore or deletion.

setup.title: Keep licences and use the project’s maintenance tools
setup.instruction: Keep project GPLv3, PCSX2-derived notices, libchdr, font/icon, renderer and other shipped component terms; they do not license the original game, optional replacement packs or third-party content. Quit the actual game and its waiting app normally before upstream replacement or data work, retain independent recovery and review/relink changed executable bytes. The reported long-session stall remains an upstream limitation; static source/archive checks do not establish native/installed, whole-game, real-save, hardware or Supported acceptance. setup.instruction: Use the official v0.1.11 Windows x64 package as one complete unit, including VagrantStory_Recompiled.exe, game.toml, bios/, assets/, mods/, licenses/ and overlay_toolchain/. The player reads original code/data from the user’s disc and locally compiles battle/menu/title overlays with bundled gcc in the background, retaining cache/; other code still uses the interpreter and TinyCC. First preparation can take an hour or more and resume later. Do not call this fully static coverage, impose a short first-use gameplay deadline or substitute an interpreter-only demo for a prepared route.

setup.instruction: Select VagrantStory_Recompiled.exe, use its full player directory as working directory and leave arguments empty to retain the ordinary integrated launcher and settings. Keep those distinct terms plus OpenBIOS, bundled GCC/Binutils/mingw-w64, TinyCC, font and other notices; a project or UI license does not replace noncommercial restrictions or license original assets. entries.name: Hi-Res Adventure #1: Mystery House (ScummVM)
entries.summary: Play Hi-Res Adventure #1: Mystery House in ScummVM using the game data from the upstream games page.

setup.title: Get ScummVM for your system
setup.instruction: On ScummVM’s downloads page, choose the Windows 64-bit ZIP, your Linux distribution’s package, or the universal macOS disk image for Intel and Apple Silicon. Keep the package’s support files with the player.

setup.title: Extract and add the game files
setup.instruction: On the ScummVM games page, find Hi-Res Adventure #1: Mystery House and choose MYSTHOUS.zip. Extract the ZIP, then use Add Game in ScummVM and select the folder you extracted the ZIP into.

setup.title: Play again from the saved target
setup.instruction: Select your saved entry in ScummVM and press Start. The entry remembers the game folder. To launch directly from a frontend, run ScummVM with the saved target ID. Use Game Options in ScummVM to change the entry later.

setup_notes.title: Find your launch target
setup_notes.instruction: ScummVM detects these files as adl:hires1. Run scummvm --list-targets to see the ID of the saved entry. Use that saved ID as the positional argument so ScummVM reuses its settings and data folder.

setup_notes.title: Update your player
setup_notes.instruction: For the Windows ZIP, you replace the runtime. A Linux distribution package updates through your package manager. The official universal macOS disk image uses ScummVM’s updater. Portcove leaves this installation and its files with you.

setup_notes.title: Keep your saves and settings
setup_notes.instruction: In Game Options, open Paths and check Save Path. If it shows Default, check Global Options. For a Default global path, use ScummVM’s documented location for your system or choose a save folder explicitly. Global Options also shows the configuration file path. Back up both before updating.

setup.title: Extract and add the game files
setup.instruction: On the ScummVM games page, find Beneath a Steel Sky and choose BASS-Floppy-1.3.zip. Extract the ZIP, then use Add Game in ScummVM and select the folder you extracted the ZIP into.

setup.title: Play again from the saved target
setup.instruction: Select your saved entry in ScummVM and press Start. The entry remembers the game folder. To launch directly from a frontend, run ScummVM with the saved target ID. Use Game Options in ScummVM to change the entry later.

setup_notes.title: Find your launch target
setup_notes.instruction: ScummVM detects these files as sky:sky. Run scummvm --list-targets to see the ID of the saved entry. Use that saved ID as the positional argument so ScummVM reuses its settings and data folder.

setup_notes.title: Update your player
setup_notes.instruction: For the Windows ZIP, you replace the runtime. A Linux distribution package updates through your package manager. The official universal macOS disk image uses ScummVM’s updater. Portcove leaves this installation and its files with you.

setup_notes.title: Keep your saves and settings
setup_notes.instruction: In Game Options, open Paths and check Save Path. If it shows Default, check Global Options. For a Default global path, use ScummVM’s documented location for your system or choose a save folder explicitly. Global Options also shows the configuration file path. Back up both before updating.

entries.name: Legend of Sword and Fairy / SDLPal (sdlpal)
entries.summary: Play The Legend of Sword and Fairy with SDLPAL and a working copy of your original game data.
entries.game_title: The Legend of Sword and Fairy

setup.title: Prepare a working copy of your game data
setup.instruction: Keep your originals safe and make a separate working copy of the matching DOS or Windows game-data folder. Extract the Windows MinGW ZIP’s sdlpal.exe into that working copy.

setup.title: Set the save path for a separate runtime
setup.instruction: For a separate runtime folder, explicitly configure an absolute SavePath before your first game session; changing GamePath alone in the Windows dialog does not change that session’s save location.

setup.title: Keep the player and save folder together
setup.instruction: Finish setup with that sdlpal.exe and the same folder as its working directory. On first Play, keep SDLPAL’s game folder pointed at this copy. This keeps the initial save folder and later launches at the same location.

setup.title: Set up the upstream Linux AppImage
setup.instruction: Open the official x86-64 AppImage with the host’s AppImage support. The v3.0.2025.0616 player needs glibc 2.34 or later. Its launcher runs inside the mounted image, so put your matching DOS or Windows data in a separate writable folder. Select that folder in the settings window before starting the game. The Linux settings dialog uses the selected game folder as the save folder and the AppImage stores sdlpal.cfg under ~/.config. Use lowercase game filenames on case-sensitive filesystems. Keep the config, data and .rpg saves backed up.

setup.title: Prepare a writable folder for the Mac app
setup.instruction: Copy Pal.app out of the official DMG into a permanent writable folder with your matching game files. The v3.0.2025.0616 bundle supports Intel and Apple Silicon and requires macOS 11 or later. The Finder launch uses the app’s enclosing folder for default game data and saves. Keep sdlpal.cfg and the .rpg saves with that working copy. If you launch the player from a terminal, start it with that same working directory.

setup.title: Choose the Android game folder
setup.instruction: Install the official SDLPAL APK and prepare a writable folder on the device or SD card containing your matching game data. Select that folder with Android’s document picker when SDLPAL requests access. Its settings use the selected game folder for both data and saves. Keep that folder, sdlpal.cfg and the .rpg saves recoverable when replacing the APK. Preserve your accessible backup before clearing data or changing to another package or signer.

setup_notes.title: Preserve your saved games
setup_notes.instruction: Back up that working folder, including its .rpg saves and sdlpal.cfg, when applying upstream updates.

limitations: Keep saves matched to the DOS or Windows data edition. Portcove does not update or back up this externally owned copy.
Back up that working folder, including its .rpg saves and sdlpal.cfg, when applying upstream updates.
For a separate runtime folder, explicitly configure an absolute SavePath before your first game session; changing GamePath alone in the Windows dialog does not change that session’s save location.
The Linux, Mac and Android packages use upstream setup and replacement. Their files and saves are outside the managed Windows profile.

entries.name: Sheep, Dog 'n' Wolf / Sheep, Dog 'n' Wolf: Rewooled (SDW-Community)
entries.summary: Explore Sheep, Dog 'n' Wolf / Sheep, Dog 'n' Wolf: Rewooled (SDW-Community) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

setup.title: Prepare your original game
setup.instruction: For the managed direct-player route, copy your own original PC Sheep, Dog ’n’ Wolf game data into game-data beside SheepD3D.exe on Windows or SheepD3D on Linux, with Levels directly inside game-data. setup.instruction: Use six separate literal argument tokens: --user-dir, the absolute path to this copy's userdata directory, --game, its absolute game directory, --module, and its absolute bin/gGRSEAF_recomp.dll path. Preserve spaces within each path token. Replace paths with your actual prepared locations; do not enter placeholders or --extract. setup.instruction: Review the program, start folder and all six launch arguments. Add it to Portcove, then choose Play. If you move this copy, review every changed path before playing again.

setup_notes.instruction: Keep game, bin including the generated module, art, module-src, work, userdata and every actual custom location together. entries.name: Street Rod / SDL3 Port
entries.summary: Use your own DOS Street Rod game data with the Windows package or a source build on Linux or Mac.

setup.title: Prepare a writable copy of your original game
setup.instruction: Use your own DOS Street Rod data, or get the free DOS files from the copyright owner through the link in the upstream guide. Keep SR.EXE, LIB1, LIB2 and HOT_DATA together in a writable Game copy. For optional Street Rod SE cars, keep SRSE.EXE and its matching data in Game/datadisk.

setup.title: Use the upstream Windows setup
setup.instruction: Extract the complete Windows x64 ZIP into its own folder and keep both executables and every DLL together. Open Street Rod.exe to choose your data and options. Choose original cars or Street Rod SE cars deliberately. The launcher uses the matching dataset for each.

setup.title: Build the direct player on Linux
setup.instruction: The reviewed release has no Linux package. Use the upstream source with a C11 compiler, CMake 3.24 or newer and SDL3 development files. From the repository root, run cmake -S srport -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSR_LAUNCHER=OFF -DCMAKE_C_STANDARD_LIBRARIES=-lm, then cmake --build build --target srport. The extra math-library flag is needed on Linux. Keep the built srport and its SDL3 runtime available. The Windows ZIP and launcher are not used on Linux.

setup.title: Build the direct player on Mac
setup.instruction: Use a C11 compiler, CMake 3.24 or newer and the macOS SDL3 framework from SDL’s official development package. Keep SDL3.framework in a stable folder. From the repository root, run cmake -S srport -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSR_LAUNCHER=OFF -DSDL3_DIR="/full/path/SDL3.framework/Resources/CMake" -DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH="/full/path/framework-folder", then cmake --build build --target srport. Replace both paths with your actual framework locations. Build on the Mac you will use, so the player matches Intel or Apple Silicon. Keep the framework folder in place after building. The Windows ZIP and launcher are not used. Native Mac game startup and saving have not been tested.

setup.title: Register the actual player in Portcove
setup.instruction: On Windows, choose srport.exe as the existing installation; on Linux or Mac, choose the built srport. Choose the player’s containing directory as the working directory. Add --game-dir and your writable game-data folder as two separate arguments. For Street Rod SE, choose the datadisk folder. Review the selected player, folder and arguments, then choose Play. The separate upstream launcher can stay open or close while its game continues.

setup_notes.title: Keep your settings and progress before replacing files
setup_notes.instruction: Back up HOTROD1.SAV through HOTROD15.SAV and hall_dat with each working dataset. Keep the original-car and datadisk-car folders separate so each retains its own progress. Copy %APPDATA%/Street Rod/settings.ini as well. Close both the player and launcher before replacing files. Portcove keeps a launch registration. You and upstream own runtime replacement and backups. Removing the registration leaves the working files and profile in place.

setup_notes.title: SDL3 development framework for Mac
setup_notes.instruction: Get the official SDL3 development download from https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases/latest. Use SDL3.framework from the macos-arm64_x86_64 folder in SDL3.xcframework. The iOS and simulator frameworks are different targets.

setup_notes.title: Other platforms
setup_notes.instruction: Windows x64 has the reviewed official package. Linux x64 uses the upstream source build described above, with no reviewed Linux package. Intel Mac and Apple Silicon use the upstream source build described above. Both native architectures were built; Mac game execution remains untested, and there is no reviewed Mac package. Android has no reviewed package or mobile host integration. Those platforms do not inherit the Windows or Linux observations.

limitations: Use your own original game files. The native port includes reconstructed original program behavior and its own separately licensed port code.

entries.name: Hexen II / uHexen2 Tweaked
entries.summary: Play Hexen II with the upstream Tweaked OpenGL player and your prepared original game files.

setup.title: Copy your original game data before Play
setup.instruction: Copy pak0.pak and pak1.pak from your own retail Hexen II installation, patched to version 1.11, into the data1 folder of the game folder you will play from, and keep your original installation separately. The engine refuses older or mixed pak versions; nothing patches them for you, and the package contains no game data or patching tools.

setup.title: Use a copy you manage yourself
setup.instruction: Extract the complete Windows test ZIP into a separate working Hexen II folder that already holds data1. Select glh2.exe with that folder, then choose Play. This is a Win32 OpenGL Hexen II preview, not HexenWorld.

setup_notes.title: Keep the game folder's saves and settings
setup_notes.instruction: Saves, configuration, demos and screenshots go to data1 inside the working folder, and startup logging can write debug_h2.log beside glh2.exe. Back up the complete folder before replacing the player in a copy you manage yourself.

setup_notes.title: Build a separate Linux demo player
setup_notes.instruction: On Linux x86-64, build the test-1 tag from engine/hexen2 with make DEMO=1 h2 and the SDL 1.2, ALSA, libmad and Vorbis development libraries. The OpenGL source target needs a header missing from the tag. Put the resulting hexen2 executable beside the complete data1 folder from Hammer of Thyrion’s November 1997 Linux AMD64 demo package. Use the whole folder, including progs.dat. Open the folder and run ./hexen2.

setup_notes.title: Keep the Linux demo profile
setup_notes.instruction: The Linux demo keeps its saves and settings in ~/.hexen2demo, separate from the Windows retail copy. Back up that profile before replacing your Linux build. The Tweaked publisher offers a Windows package. Intel and Apple Silicon Mac binaries and an Android package are unavailable for this fork’s release.

limitations: The test package bundles ten third-party codec and runtime DLLs without their licence notices. Portcove downloads the package only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files.

Portal of Praevus, HexenWorld and mods are not part of this route; they need other programs, folders or arguments in a copy you manage yourself. Portal of Praevus needs portals/pak3.pak and the -portals argument.

entries.name: Teeworlds
entries.summary: Swing through 2D arenas, play local and online matches, and create your own maps.
entries.download_block_reason: Choose a download from the Teeworlds project or install the game through your package manager.

setup.title: Add the Windows client to Portcove
setup.instruction: After extracting the complete official Windows x64 ZIP, select teeworlds.exe and its containing folder. Keep the data folder and the accompanying files together. Leave launch options empty, review the details, and add the game. Choose Play separately. teeworlds_srv.exe is the dedicated server, not the client.

setup.title: Add the Linux client to Portcove
setup.instruction: Select the teeworlds client from your complete Linux x64 package and use its containing folder as the start folder. A distribution package normally installs it at /usr/games/teeworlds; install its data package and dependencies through the same package manager. Leave launch options empty. Update the installation through upstream or your package manager. The separate community Flathub client is available on Linux x64 and ARM64; install and update that copy through Flatpak rather than selecting a Flatpak launcher as a native executable.

setup.title: Add the Intel Mac client to Portcove
setup.instruction: Copy the complete Teeworlds.app from the publisher disk image into Applications and open it normally once. In Portcove, select /Applications/Teeworlds.app/Contents/MacOS/teeworlds, use its containing folder as the start folder, and leave launch options empty. Keep the complete app bundle together. Teeworlds Server.app is a separate dedicated server. The later teeworlds.exe choice applies to Windows; Mac uses the native file inside Teeworlds.app. The bundled 0.7.5 Intel runtime requires macOS 10.13 or later; Portcove has its own system requirements.

setup.title: Play and record a match
setup.instruction: The Teeworlds 0.7 client connects to Teeworlds 0.7 servers. In a match, press F1 and enter record followed by a demo name. Enter stoprecord to finish, then open the recording from Demos.

setup.title: Select the prepared player
setup.instruction: Select teeworlds.exe and use its containing folder as the working directory. Leave arguments empty. Keep the complete independently permitted runtime and finish the title-specific preparation before Play.

setup_notes.title: Find your data folder
setup_notes.instruction: The defaults are %APPDATA%/Teeworlds on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Teeworlds on Mac, and ~/.local/share/teeworlds on Linux. On Linux, the game prefers an existing ~/.teeworlds folder or uses $XDG_DATA_HOME/teeworlds if XDG_DATA_HOME is set. For the Flathub installation, check ~/.var/app/com.teeworlds.Teeworlds/.teeworlds. If you changed storage.cfg, use its save location.

setup_notes.title: Registration ownership and removal
setup_notes.instruction: Portcove records the selected executable, working folder and literal arguments after review. Play is separate and only the selected process is supervised. You and upstream own replacement and updates; relink changed executable bytes after reviewing them. Removing this registration preserves every external file. Managed installation, backup, rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for this external copy.

setup_notes.title: Player-data ownership
setup_notes.instruction: You and upstream own the external copy's data: Windows %APPDATA%/Teeworlds settings07.cfg, demos, maps and skins; Linux ~/.local/share/teeworlds, existing ~/.teeworlds or $XDG_DATA_HOME/teeworlds; Intel Mac ~/Library/Application Support/Teeworlds and any storage.cfg save path; the save location selected by storage.cfg, and any custom maps or skins kept with the installation. Back up these locations separately; registration does not migrate or certify their compatibility.

limitations: Before moving your setup, close the game and copy the data folder with settings07.cfg, demos, custom maps, and any skins you want to keep.

setup.instruction: Use a complete player and components you are independently permitted to use, with your own The Darkness Xbox 360 USA/Europe (En/Fr/De/Es/It), title 545407EE. setup.instruction: The inspected official 0.9.8 Windows ZIP contains AMD64 TheDarkness.exe, separate TheDarknessSettings.exe and matching runtime libraries/notices. setup.instruction: The normal root is the Windows Saved Games location, usually %USERPROFILE%/Saved Games/Estacado, with TheDarkness.pc.toml, content/ saves and other player data. Per-user logs, caches and diagnostics also use the separate %LOCALAPPDATA%/Estacado root (or the runtime’s actual local fallback); preserve it too. An already existing portable.txt beside TheDarkness.exe instead keeps the legacy package-local configuration/runtime_data; explicit external config/user-data roots also remain authoritative. setup.instruction: Quit the actual game normally before upstream replacement, importing old saves, changing game data or updating mods/settings. setup.title: Read the build instructions
setup.instruction: Follow the project’s instructions for build_from_xci.sh. You need your own Tears of the Kingdom 1.0.0 XCI and prod.keys. Portcove does not build or launch this project.

setup_notes.title: November 4, 2026 research notes
setup_notes.instruction: An experimental Tears of the Kingdom Linux x86-64 port translating AArch64 main and parts of the SDK to C++ with native services and NVN-to-Vulkan support. The separate zeldaret matching-decompilation project does not establish its playability. The author reports one Steam Deck outdoor walk at 62–64 FPS, rather than full-game stability or completion. First start warms shaders; faster code generation is planned. A PC clang O2 build took 17 minutes elapsed and 2.1 CPU hours; a one-to-1.5-hour Deck estimate is unmeasured. There are no release files. Use build_from_xci.sh to import, generate, compile and package privately; the launcher’s game-build button is not connected, so the command line is required. Build requirements include exactly Capstone 5.0.9, 16 GB RAM and 45 GB peak disk. Linux x86-64 needs AVX2 on Haswell/Zen 2 or newer; distrobox Ubuntu 24.04 or Linux PC builds are documented. Windows/macOS are unconfirmed. Supply your own version 1.0.0 cartridge XCI, title 0100F2C0115B6000, main build ID 082CE09B06E33A12 and prod.keys with master-key revision 0x0E. Other versions are unsupported; separate firmware and exact regional hashes are unspecified. Portcove offers no setup or launch integration and has not tested gameplay.

limitations: The documented build needs 16 GB RAM and up to 45 GB of disk space. The Linux x86-64 version needs AVX2.

entries.name: The Operative: No One Lives Forever (GOTY) (NOLF1 Modern / nolfsrc)
entries.summary: Research listing. Upstream route: Public release archive plus owned-disc import; native Windows, Wine/Proton elsewhere Limits: Alpha native Windows rebuilt engine; clean public archive/owned-disc route only, retail-image-fetching submodule workflow excluded. Upstream platforms: Native Windows public archive/source build; Linux/macOS use Wine/Proton rather than native builds. Selected Windows executable CPU architecture unknown in frozen research. entries.game_title: The Operative: No One Lives Forever (GOTY)

setup.title: Prepare the clean public modern copy with your own GOTY discs
setup.instruction: Use an already permitted complete native Windows NOLF Modern copy prepared from the clean public archive in a new empty directory with your own two European Game of the Year Edition disc images, corresponding to the documented redump discs 42823 and 42561. Complete upstream installation/checksum verification outside Portcove. The original-data-fetching rez submodule workflow is excluded. Other regions/editions do not inherit this setup. Nightly builds and alpha releases must be chosen deliberately; no original image, installer, compiler or game helper is run here.

setup.title: Select the direct player that waits for the game
setup.instruction: Select normal NOLF.exe in the completed Windows game directory, keeping all companion binaries and established settings. The selected modern direct entry sets its working directory to its own folder and waits for its lithtech.exe child, retaining that process lifetime. NOLFLauncher.exe is the separate configuration launcher; do not substitute a setup batch file or a launcher that merely hands off and exits. Linux/macOS paths use Wine/Proton/CrossOver and are not native platform qualifications here.

setup.title: Keep the whole creating installation and permitted components
setup.instruction: Retain Save/, autoexec.cfg, launcher.ini, nolfcmds.txt, logs including modern.log/nolfsrc.log, captures, custom files and the complete old installation. Upstream says each new archive is a whole installation, not an overlay patch; preserve the old copy and deliberately copy compatible saves into a separately completed new copy before relinking. Monolith/GameSpy, OpenMiles GPL, Bink/FFmpeg LGPL and DirectMusic have distinct terms; the upstream license notes retain distribution-compatibility questions. A public download or engine-code license is not a whole-package/IP grant, and this guide does not infer a blanket ban on an independently permitted copy.

setup.title: Review the prepared player and launch details
setup.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools, then start and quit the permitted copy you intend to add. Keep its game executable, working folder and supported launch arguments. Review those details in Portcove and agree to launch them, then choose Play separately. Adding a copy does not confirm its original game files, gameplay or save compatibility.

setup.title: Retain upstream replacement and external ownership
setup.instruction: Close every running copy of the game before changing files. Keep the working game version and every original-file, profile and data location it uses. Update it with the project’s tools, then review and select the changed executable in Portcove. You manage setup, replacement, file changes, data migration and recovery. Portcove monitors the process you selected; it does not restrict file access or prevent other copies from running. Removing the registration leaves external files in place. This route does not offer Portcove downloads, setup, updates, backups, rollback, data migration or external-file deletion.

limitations: Use only a copy and components you are already permitted to use. Engine licensing does not grant original-game, music, mod, middleware or redistribution rights.
Before changing versions, keep a copy of the working game and every data and profile folder it uses. Another executable may use those same folders.

setup.title: Choose the original once
setup.instruction: Open The Order 1886, then select the supported extracted PS4 game on Game & Content. Use game update 1.02, required for v0.2.33. entries.name: The Settlers / FreeSerf
entries.summary: Build a settlement in FreeSerf using your own DOS or Amiga game data.

setup.title: Choose data from your original game
setup.instruction: Use your original DOS data file SPAE.PA, SPAD.PA, SPAF.PA or SPAU.PA, or the six original Amiga files listed in the upstream guide. Copy them to ~/.local/share/freeserf on Linux or Mac, or to the freeserf folder under %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows, and keep your originals separate. When launching from a terminal, -g takes the directory containing your data.

setup.title: Install the Windows or Mac release
setup.instruction: On Windows x64, use the Release installer. On Apple Silicon with macOS 26 or later, copy FreeSerf.app from the DMG. Set up your original data before opening the player.

setup.title: Keep your saves and settings
setup.instruction: FreeSerf keeps saves, including Ctrl+Z quicksaves and the optional autosave, in freeserf/saves under XDG_DATA_HOME on Linux, or in ~/freeserf/saves when XDG_DATA_HOME is unset. On Windows it uses the freeserf folder in your Saved Games folder, and on Mac Library/Application Support/freeserf/saves. Settings are in freeserf.ini: in ~/.local/share/freeserf or under XDG_DATA_HOME on Linux, in %APPDATA%\freeserf on Windows, and in Library/Application Support/freeserf on Mac. These stay in place when the player is replaced. Use -l with a saved game file to reopen it.

limitations: The v0.5 Mac DMG requires Apple Silicon. The publisher does not provide an Intel Mac or Android package in this release.

This documented entry uses the same preparation checks, settings, save protection and environment as the upstream Play button, then waits for game_proc. It starts the matching game with explicit game-data and user-data roots; do not substitute an extractor, private helper or the Linux script. Keep the established Windows C++ and graphics driver dependencies.

setup.title: Check which game sessions are still running
setup.instruction: The supported --play launcher waits for its normal game process. Upstream owns its independent update mechanism: it may replace launcher/engine files and ask you to restart, or leave a separately named new launcher if replacement fails. Close actual players and companions before deliberate replacement; preserve old working files, then review and relink changed selected bytes. This registration does not invoke, authenticate or manage that updater.

setup.title: Review Play and preserve external ownership
setup.instruction: Review and consent to the exact selected native executable, established CWD and literal arguments, then choose Play separately. Upstream and you own preparation, runtime replacement and recovery. Removing registration preserves every external file. Portcove offers no external update, backup, rollback, migration or deletion. Close actual players and companions, keep the old complete working copy and every effective data root, then review and relink changed selected bytes.

setup_notes.title: Retain the complete creating copy and actual data
setup_notes.instruction: Keep the complete runtime, gamedata and every effective data root. Windows player saves/cache default to %LOCALAPPDATA%/simpsons with a home/AppData/Local fallback; the launcher passes that effective path explicitly. simpsons.toml is beside the game executable. Preserve launcher.json, art, mods, backups, diagnostics, logs, shader caches, native shaders and any custom engine/lib/data configuration. Upstream Play may repair saves and create backups; those operations remain upstream-owned, not Portcove backup/rollback promises. Keep private profiles and credentials private. Project GPLv3, ReXGlue/Xenia BSD-3-Clause, XenonRecomp MIT and other notices remain separate from the original game and assets.

limitations: Use only an actual copy and components you are permitted to use. Preserve all originals, runtime companions, saves, settings, mods, caches, logs, backups and custom roots. Another executable may share them. Static source/metadata and reusable fixtures are not gameplay, real-save, installed-client, Supported or protected acceptance.

entries.name: Quake 4 (openQ4)
entries.summary: A beta openQ4 player using your own legitimate installed PC Quake 4 and matching data. Engine GPL and game SDK terms apply separately; keep all notices and do not treat package availability as permission for every component. Exact accepted original revision/hashes and BIOS/firmware needs are unconfirmed. You and the project manage setup and replacement; Portcove has not qualified a release package or confirmed gameplay.

setup.title: Use your own PC Quake 4 installation
setup.instruction: Use the official v0.13.2 Windows x64 package and a legitimate supported PC Quake 4 installation, such as Steam or GOG. This is the PC engine route, not the Xbox 360 recompilation or a standalone replacement for original assets. Keep all selected package/components you are independently permitted to use and the original installation.

setup.title: Keep the complete client and game modules
setup.instruction: Retain openQ4-client_x64.exe, OpenAL/renderer libraries, baseoq4/ with its SP/MP game modules and runtime packages, docs and notices together. The separate openQ4-ded_x64.exe is a server, not normal Play. Retail game assets remain under the original installation’s q4base/; do not copy them into baseoq4/. The selected player route uses OpenGL by default; experimental Vulkan, Windows ARM64, Linux/Deck and macOS claims remain separate, unobserved qualifications.

setup.title: Attach the native client with its retail root
setup.instruction: Select openQ4-client_x64.exe, use its complete extracted package root as working directory, and set +set fs_basepath "the actual PC Quake 4 root containing q4base". Review the exact path and intent and choose Play when ready. Point at the root, not q4base/ or baseoq4/. Retain any already chosen supported fs_savepath or mod configuration rather than selecting a new profile. Quit the client normally before ending the session; developer, replay and dedicated-server modes do not replace ordinary Play.

setup.title: Preserve the actual openQ4 save root and compatibility
setup.instruction: The selected Windows source normally resolves Known LocalAppData/openQ4, with environment/Saved Games fallbacks; +set fs_savepath can select an existing explicit root. Keep the actual resolved root, configs, saves/screenshots, logs, mods, cache and recovery, plus legacy/stock Quake 4 saves separately. The current policy writes v3 and gates an exact wire ABI, verified build floor and integrity; it rejects v2, newer payloads and unsupported ABI tuples. Format eligibility is not runtime certification, and stock/old/cross-platform saves are not automatically compatible. No save conversion, restore, merge or deletion is performed.

setup.title: Keep distinct licenses and upstream replacement
setup.instruction: Engine code is GPLv3 with retained Doom 3/Doom 3 BFG notices and accompanying Additional Terms. The openQ4-game libraries are Quake 4 SDK-derived and retain the SDK EULA; original Quake 4 assets have separate ownership. Retain all accompanying terms; the provenance inventory is an engineering record, not a blanket permission or compatibility conclusion. Upstream/player owns runtime replacement and recovery: finish updates outside a session, preserve data and review/relink changed bytes. No campaign, physical controller, multiplayer, installed/native, Supported or managed install/update/rollback/backup/deletion acceptance is asserted.

limitations: Select the native x64 client and point fs_basepath at the PC Quake 4 root. Keep q4base and baseoq4 separate; preserve the actual save root and do not infer stock, legacy or cross-platform save compatibility.

setup.instruction: Select Phase Distorter.exe, choose its complete extracted Windows release folder as working directory and leave arguments empty to use the remembered/default game and upstream import UI. Import leaves originals and the executable unchanged; later starts use the locally imported pack. Do not select a headless, coverage or experimental native-session command as the ordinary player.

A new release can find an old import in this external folder; that does not mean the download contains original game data.

entries.name: Thrill Drive 2 / Konami Viper
entries.summary: Build a native Thrill Drive 2 player from your own arcade game and Konami Viper board dumps with the project's setup package.

setup.title: Build your game once
setup.instruction: Extract the package. Put your own supported Thrill Drive 2 EBB, JAA or AAA game files and the kviper board files in roms (941b01.u25 and the ds2430.u3 EEPROM). Include the matching CHD and NVRAM files listed by the project. Run viper-setup.exe on Windows or viper-setup from the package folder on Linux or Mac. Setup builds a player from the files it recognizes.

setup.title: Open the generated player
setup.instruction: After setup succeeds, open the player for your original. td2 for EBB, td2j for JAA or td2a for AAA. On Windows the player has an .exe extension. Open the same player on later launches. Use Options for settings. The --classic option starts the arcade mode.

setup_notes.title: Keep saves when replacing the package
setup_notes.instruction: Keep the NVRAM saves and settings beside the generated player, including its separate enhanced and classic saves. Back up that folder before replacing the release, then run the upstream setup again for the new version. Portcove does not replace the generated runtime or back up its data.

setup_notes.title: Use the upstream command line
setup_notes.instruction: For the default release variant, run viper-setup --prepare --roms with your original-files folder followed by thrild2. Watch the progress lines and wait for success. Then viper-setup --play thrild2 starts the generated player and returns its exit status. Exit code 66 means the upstream setup has no built game for that variant.

limitations: The release package contains a builder. You supply the original game files and board BIOS.

setup.instruction: With the game closed, copy %APPDATA%/TuxRacer on Windows or ~/.tuxracer on Linux and Mac. Keep that backup when replacing your extracted game folder. Extreme Tux Racer uses a different profile.

setup.instruction: The game writes tux_sshot_*.ppm and its optional diagnostic_log.txt beside the player. In an extracted copy, keep those files when replacing the runtime. Move screenshots you want to keep before playing again, because the game restarts screenshot numbering at zero.

entries.name: UFO: Enemy Unknown / X-COM: UFO Defense (OpenXcom)
entries.summary: Set up UFO: Enemy Unknown / X-COM: UFO Defense through its upstream OpenXcom player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.
entries.game_title: UFO: Enemy Unknown / X-COM: UFO Defense

setup.title: Use this original game and edition
setup.instruction: Use your own complete unmodified original UFO/XCOM data folders. XcomUtil-modified originals can fail. Copy the original subfolders into OpenXcom’s UFO subdirectory, keeping their hierarchy; TFTD files are not UFO data. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files.

setup.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
setup.instruction: Use the official upstream download/setup route or a complete already prepared OpenXcom player, keeping its common data and standard mod resources. No GitHub release package was observed. Complete original-data and game selection through upstream before saving the player entry. On Windows, register openxcom.exe with its installation folder as working directory, retaining the upstream game selection rather than inventing a fixed argument. The upstream Windows installer may copy a detected Steam original when you deliberately run it.

setup.title: Add the game and manage your files
setup.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Portcove saves your selected executable, working folder and launch arguments; choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, original files and profile. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions.

setup.title: Choose the Windows nightly package
setup.instruction: In OpenXcom’s Nightly GitHub workflow, choose a successful upstream run. On Windows x64 download the Windows artifact, then extract the inner win64 ZIP into a dedicated folder. Keep its DLLs and data directories with OpenXcom.exe and open the player from that folder. The same artifact offers a separate win32 ZIP and an upstream installer.

setup.title: Choose the Linux or Mac nightly package
setup.instruction: In the same workflow run, download the matching artifact. On Linux unpack the ZIP and start the AppImage. If the loader reports libjack.so.0 missing, install your distribution’s JACK runtime package. On Mac unpack the outer ZIP and use Mac Archive Utility on the inner Mac ZIP, then open openxcom.app on Intel or Apple Silicon. On Linux x86-64, select the complete official Nightly AppImage and its containing folder. Provide the host JACK and PipeWire libraries required by the package. If FUSE is unavailable, enter --appimage-extract-and-run as a separate first argument. On Intel or Apple Silicon Mac, keep openxcom.app intact and select Contents/MacOS/openxcom with its containing folder. On Linux and Mac, enter -master and xcom1 as separate arguments, after --appimage-extract-and-run when you use it. Confirm the selected original and master game upstream before saving the registration. Use separate writable -user and -cfg folders for each game when you want to keep the profiles apart. Enter each option and its absolute path on separate lines.

setup.title: Prepare this title’s original data
setup.instruction: Copy the data subfolders from your UFO: Enemy Unknown or X-COM: UFO Defense installation into UFO inside the OpenXcom data or user folder. In the OpenXcom Mods menu, select the master game for this title.

setup_notes.title: Keep your originals and game data
setup_notes.instruction: Windows normally uses the actual Documents/OpenXcom user/config location; an installation-local user folder and explicit -data/-user/-config choices can change the searched locations. Preserve every actual selected data/user/config folder, including UFO/TFTD resources, mods, savegames and screenshots. Keep the two original games and their campaigns distinct even if they share one player/profile. Back up with OpenXcom closed before changing runtime or mods.

setup_notes.title: Back up the actual OpenXcom profile
setup_notes.instruction: On Linux back up the active user and config folders shown in openxcom.log. The user folder can be ~/.local/share/openxcom or ~/.openxcom. Also keep ~/.config/openxcom or any XDG or command-line overrides. On Mac keep ~/Library/Application Support/OpenXcom or the configured XDG directory. Preserve originals, settings, mods and saves before replacing an upstream nightly.

limitations: Keep the two original games and their campaigns distinct even if they share one player/profile. Back up with OpenXcom closed before changing runtime or mods.

setup.instruction: Choose the official Windows installer from Exult’s download page, or keep a complete upstream-prepared player with its runtime data. setup.title: Set up the upstream Linux package
setup.instruction: Install info.exult.exult from Flathub and open it once to create its sandbox folders. Put this game’s own STATIC directory in ~/.var/app/info.exult.exult/data/serpentisle or configure the actual working path. Preserve the sandbox config, serpentisle data, saves and gamedat. A native non-Flatpak Exult uses a separate profile, normally ~/.exult.cfg and ~/.exult/serpentisle. On Linux x86-64, install the Ubuntu 26.04 exult package; version 1.12.1 was checked. Prepare this game’s configuration with that package first. Select /usr/lib/games/exult/exult and a private working folder. Do not select the packaged exult launcher script, because it can split arguments that contain spaces. Enter -c, the absolute path to your prepared configuration, and --si on separate argument lines. Start Flatpak copies through their upstream route.

setup.title: Prepare the official Mac app
setup.instruction: Use Exult’s official Intel/Apple Silicon DMG. Keep the complete app and point it to your own Serpent Isle installation. The documented default original folder is /Library/Application Support/Exult/serpentisle. Back up ~/Library/Preferences/exult.cfg, ~/Library/Application Support/exult/serpentisle, and every custom savegame, gamedat and mod location before replacing the app. On Intel or Apple Silicon Mac, keep the official Exult.app intact and select Contents/MacOS/exult and its containing folder. Enter -c and the absolute path to your prepared Exult configuration as separate arguments, followed by --si. Use the configuration for the matching original and preserve its actual save and gamedat locations before changing players.

setup.instruction: Choose the official Android APK under the stable release on Exult’s download page and check its Android version requirement. Exult installs the files in its app-private serpentisle/static directory. Keep your original ZIP separately. It does not contain Exult’s settings or saves. entries.name: Vagrant Story (PS1) (VS-NativePort)
entries.summary: A source-only Vagrant Story Windows x86-64 C++ port reaching the opening, prologue and selected combat systems. Audio, full abilities and equipment remain incomplete. No ready-made player release is established. Supply your own USA SLUS-01040 BIN/CUE and follow the conversion script instructions. Portcove has not confirmed setup or gameplay.

setup.title: Use the full experimental Windows tester package
setup.instruction: Keep VS-NativePort-0.0.11-win-x64.zip intact with VS.Launcher.exe, VS.Desktop.exe, VS.Extract.exe, runtime DLLs, resources, licenses and release.json. This is an unfinished Vagrant Story port for Windows 10 1903+/11 x64, with gameplay, cutscene, rendering and audio limits. Native game saves and memory-card/ending conversion are different contracts; complete original memory-card support is not established. No finished-game, native/controller, real-save or Supported acceptance is claimed.

setup.title: Complete the upstream exact-disc and converter checks
setup.instruction: Supply your own USA SLUS-01040 single-track MODE2/2352 disc as BIN, supported CUE/BIN or parentless single-data-track CHD. The decompressed BIN must be exactly 750,643,152 bytes, SHA-256 25221D7F8FDB2C4490AF12D9E82F0E58BDD6ACB43387F9082B3C5E79DFE090C0, SHA-1 38C63DB6C49A06B91D87CD5A4E31B1EC68FE212C. A matching name is insufficient; CHD hashes apply to its decoded content, not container bytes. Complete upstream Start-Game.cmd dependency checks and launcher setup first, including an explicitly chosen compatible FFmpeg with the required encoders. Software installation and original/converter acquisition remain separate user/upstream actions, not Portcove operations.

setup.title: Add the ordinary native launcher
setup.instruction: Select VS.Launcher.exe in the complete tester folder, use that containing folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the selected program, folder and arguments, then choose Play when ready. Use the upstream disc, save-folder and converter pickers and its Play control. The launcher verifies the full image for each Play, prepares assets and starts VS.Desktop.exe with their context. Do not substitute VS.Extract.exe, Start-Game.cmd, a converter, or context-free VS.Desktop.exe as the same route; no integrity refusal is bypassed.

setup.title: Keep per-user prepared assets and separately selected saves
setup.instruction: Preserve the full %APPDATA%/VS-NativePort/VagrantStory directory with prepared assets, completion inventories, launcher selections, logs and retained failed/replaced staging as present. Also retain the exact game-save folder you selected, including slot00.vssave through slot99.vssave and recoverable .bak files as present; it is independent of installed program files and prepared assets. Keep the original disc available for later verification and preserve custom --save-dir choices. Do not delete retained failure directories, merge original memory cards or reset path selections to register the game. Portcove performs no source conversion, save migration, backup or restore.

setup.title: Leave updater and recovery ownership upstream
setup.instruction: The launcher owns its offered update checks, consent and replacement/recovery flow; registration does not select an update or install FFmpeg. Quit the actual game/helpers before maintenance or recovery, retain prior complete program/data/save copies and review/select the current launcher after changes. Portcove observes the selected launcher only; a finished activity does not prove all child processes stopped. Removing its reference preserves external files. Managed installation/update/backup/rollback, full-session tracking and Supported qualification are not offered. CC0 project terms, retained earlier GPL grants, third-party libraries and original-game rights remain separate.

limitations: Select VS.Launcher.exe in the complete Windows tester package after upstream dependency/disc setup. Keep the exact USA image, %APPDATA%/VS-NativePort/VagrantStory assets and independently selected save folder; experimental limits and original memory-card conversion remain explicit.

entries.name: Valkyrie Profile / ValkyrieRecomp
entries.summary: Locally prepared Valkyrie Profile player using your own USA two-disc CUE/BIN set: SLUS-01156 and SLUS-01179. Complete generation, firmware choice and settings upstream, then select the finished native product rather than its forwarding setup host. Between-run disc selection does not establish mid-session swapping.

setup.title: Prepare the supported USA two-disc original
setup.instruction: Use your own Valkyrie Profile USA discs, Disc 1 SLUS-01156 and Disc 2 SLUS-01179, as complete CUE/BIN sets. The selected game.toml identifies Disc 1 data Track 01 by size 730448880 bytes and SHA1 fa13cbde448a47fa87b6c7829df1c5e6215f5f66; this is not a Disc 2 or whole-set fingerprint. The source lists both discs in a roster and boots the first program. Complete original selection, local generation/build, firmware selection and settings through the official v1.0.1 upstream setup before attachment.

setup.title: Keep the completed product and setup tree
setup.instruction: The selected setup configuration generates BIOS/game C from the owner’s inputs and builds the product under build-release/ by default. Keep the complete source/setup tree, toolchain, originals, generated output and the product’s BIOS/mods/assets/settings together. Existing project/build-root overrides remain upstream choices. Do not confuse the initial package’s ValkyrieRecomp.exe with the completed native game of the same name: the setup host starts the product as a successor and exits.

setup.title: Attach the native product directly
setup.instruction: Select the actual completed build-release/ValkyrieRecomp.exe, or the product at the installation’s already chosen build-root override. Use its complete product directory as working directory and leave arguments empty after upstream configuration. Review the selected program, working folder and arguments and choose Play when ready. The selected shared setup consumer disables forwarding in a full game binary with game dispatch; direct product selection retains the actual native session. Do not select the initial forwarding setup host, recompiler or diagnostic mode. Finish rebuilds outside a running session and quit the actual game normally.

setup.title: Preserve both discs, roster and memory cards
setup.instruction: Keep the full prepared tree, both original CUE/BIN sets, game.toml disc roster, remembered disc index/selection, settings.toml, BIOS/disc sidecars, input/mod configuration and all active saves/card1.mcd and card2.mcd or explicit slot/root overrides. Relative Windows paths anchor to the native executable directory. Upstream supports disc selection between runs; mid-session swapping is not established and is explicitly unfinished in the selected game configuration. Do not claim a complete multi-disc playthrough, merge cards or replace a populated product root with fresh setup files. No card migration, restore or deletion is performed.

setup.title: Keep component and ownership limits
setup.instruction: Retain exact psxrecomp PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, recomp-ui MIT, chosen BIOS, font, compiler and all other component notices; these do not license the original game or artwork. Only use a complete independently permitted player/component set. Upstream/player owns generation, rebuilds and replacement: preserve data/recovery and review/relink changed bytes after maintenance. Work-in-progress compatibility and hardware claims remain distinct from this attachment route. No native/installed, real-save restore, full campaign/disc-swap, Supported or managed lifecycle acceptance is asserted.

limitations: Attach the completed product EXE, not its forwarding setup host. Preserve both original discs and actual cards; between-run disc selection does not establish mid-session swaps or a full multi-disc playthrough.

setup.instruction: Review and consent to the exact executable, initial working directory and empty argument list. Registration does not build or launch the game; choose Play explicitly. setup.instruction: Keep the entire actual runtime and %LOCALAPPDATA%/Verdite2 profile, or its established override: settings.json including CdPath/CardAPath/CardBPath, interface.ini, carda.sav/cardb.sav and backup/damaged companions, mods including mods/.cache and profile-root .mods-seeded, builds including KingsField2.dll and profile-root build.log, update.json, icon files, crashes, dumps/diagnostics and all unknown/custom paths. setup.instruction: Keep data/, saves/, slot1.vzs, options.cfg, vz.sco and benchmark-results/ with the player. Portcove keeps them across managed updates. If you keep a copy you manage yourself, back them up before replacing the player. Keep any resource folder, save file or options file you chose with --data, VURUS_DATA_DIR, --save-file or --options-file.

setup_notes.title: Set up the upstream PortMaster build on an ARM64 handheld
setup_notes.instruction: Use compatible ARM64 firmware with PortMaster installed, SDL 2.0.18 or newer and native OpenGL ES 3.0. Get vurus-portmaster.zip from https://github.com/rzrbld/vurus/releases/tag/portmaster-v202611031626-beta. Extract Vurus.sh, Vurus Benchmark.sh and vurus/ together into the firmware’s Ports folder.

setup_notes.title: Import and preserve your handheld data
setup_notes.instruction: Place your own ISO or single-BIN CUE and its BIN beside vurus.aarch64, or copy an existing data/ import there. Start Vurus from the firmware’s Ports menu. Back up data/, saves/, slot1.vzs, options.cfg and vz.sco before applying an upstream update. Keep these files when updating the engine in place. You manage this copy.

limitations: The managed routes use the desktop beta packages. The separate PortMaster package needs compatible handheld firmware. There is no Android APK or general-purpose Linux ARM64 desktop package in this release.

setup.instruction: In the launcher, choose Browse and select your own unmodified US Game Boy Advance ROM. The launcher checks for an 8 MiB file with game code AWAE and MD5 5fe47355a33e3fabec2a1607af88a404. Choose Launch Game.

setup.title: Select the prepared Windows player
setup.instruction: Select wl4-launcher.exe and use its containing folder as the working directory. Leave arguments empty. Keep the complete independently permitted runtime and finish the title-specific preparation before Play.

setup_notes.title: Registration ownership and removal
setup_notes.instruction: Portcove records the selected executable, working folder and literal arguments after review. Play is separate and only the selected process is supervised. setup_notes.instruction: You and upstream own the external copy's data: Windows %APPDATA%\wl4\wl4.sav and settings.cfg; the Windows user registry entry for the original ROM path; Linux ~/.local/share/biorhythmicstudios/warioland4/ and ~/.config/biorhythmicstudios/warioland4/ (or your XDG overrides).
