setup.title: Open the Windows archive
setup.instruction: Choose the publisher archive for x64, ARM64 or x86 Windows. Extract it to its own writable folder, keep bin and data together and open bin/warzone2100.exe. To keep the game profile in the extracted tree, create an empty .portable file beside the executable before first launch.

setup.title: Install through upstream on Linux
setup.instruction: On Ubuntu 26.04 x64 or ARM64, install warzone2100 from the Ubuntu package repository and open it from your app menu. On Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 x64, you can install the publisher’s matching DEB through your package manager. The publisher also offers the net.wz2100.wz2100 Flatpak for Linux x64 and ARM64.

setup.title: Open the Mac application
setup.instruction: Extract the publisher's universal ZIP and open Warzone 2100.app on an Intel or Apple Silicon Mac. The Intel player targets macOS 10.14 or later. Apple Silicon and the bundled Vulkan renderer require macOS 11 or later.

setup.title: Keep your campaign progress and custom content
setup.instruction: In Options, open the actual Configuration Directory and back it up before replacing the game. Keep savegames, config, custom maps, mods and replays together, including any custom profile location. Ubuntu DEBs and the no-video Mac archive omit the campaign videos. Follow the publisher's video instructions if you want them.

setup_notes.title: Register the publisher Linux player with Portcove CLI
setup_notes.instruction: Use warzone-2100-official-maintained-source-port as the port ID in external select-preview and external select. For the extracted publisher Ubuntu x64 DEB, select the absolute usr/bin/warzone2100 path and set --working-directory to its usr/bin folder. Pass the absolute usr/share/warzone2100 directory as --arg=--datadir=<path> and your absolute profile path as --arg=--configdir=<path>. Quote each full argument if it contains spaces. Repeat the details with external select and pass the preview SHA-256 to --expected-preview. Start with portcove exec and the same port ID.

setup_notes.title: Keep the Ubuntu package’s campaign files
setup_notes.instruction: The Ubuntu 26.04 repository package starts through its own sandboxed launcher. Its default profile is ~/.local/share/warzone2100. Close the game before copying your campaign saves and other player data. When switching from a separately installed copy of the same release, keep the original backup until the loaded campaign is working.

limitations: The upstream desktop player can register a handler for Discord join links when it starts. The publisher Linux package writes the handler and MIME association outside its selected profile. Removing a Portcove registration leaves those files in place. Package replacement and backups are player-managed.

Supported .z64/.v64/.n64 byte orders are normalized before that runtime check; their raw file digests are not interchangeable. This is source matching, not ownership or package authentication. setup.instruction: The inspected official 0.8.1 Windows ZIP contains wg3d-recomp-v0.8.1/wg3d.exe as an AMD64 player with matching renderer/runtime libraries and notices. Keep the complete folder. setup.instruction: Select wg3d.exe, use the complete extracted package directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the exact intent and request Play separately, then use the upstream UI to start the already selected game. Finish missing-ROM setup outside the attached attempt.

setup.title: Preserve Roaming data and the actual Controller Paks
setup.instruction: Keep the whole active data root, normally %APPDATA%/WG3DRecomp on Windows, including the validated ROM copy, settings/input/window files, logs/wg3d.log and saves/controllerpak_port<N>/ for the corresponding controller ports. An already established --data-dir can choose an external root; preserve that exact directory too. The source declares no cartridge save type and routes saves to Controller Paks; do not replace them with another title’s EEPROM file or infer real save compatibility. This guide performs no import, migration, backup or deletion.

setup.instruction: Keep the own-code license and all N64ModernRuntime, N64Recomp, RT64, renderer/audio/UI and font notices. They do not license the original Midway game or other titles, ROM revisions or mod content. Use only a complete copy you are independently permitted to use. Four controller ports and Controller Pak options in source are not physical-device, multiplayer or card import/restore acceptance; those observations remain separate.

setup.title: Maintain the external copy explicitly
setup.instruction: Quit the actual game normally before upstream replacement, ROM changes or Controller Pak operations. Preserve independent recovery copies and review/relink changed executable bytes; forced termination is not a save-flush guarantee. Upstream playability/input/audio reports remain upstream claims, with no native/installed-app, full-game, save/reload or Supported acceptance asserted. Removing registration preserves external files; managed install/update/rollback/backup/removal remain unavailable.

limitations: Use USA V1.0 and the actual WG3DRecomp data root. Controller Pak storage, other revisions, devices and real save compatibility remain distinct.

entries.name: WipEout Omega Collection — wipeout_pc (AbdelmoumenDeghbouche)
entries.summary: An experimental port of WipEout Omega Collection for owned PS4 game files, with a documented US target of CUSA07671 and update 01.07. The publisher offers a Windows ZIP and Linux x86-64 AppImage and reports HD and 2048 races. A full collection playthrough remains unconfirmed.

setup.instruction: Use your own PS4 WipEout Omega Collection dump. Merge your own base and update files or supply GOW3_PATCH_DIR as documented. GoldHEN folder dumps are also supported by the instructions. The runtime reads your eboot.bin and game files and links your libc, Fios2 and NpToolkit2. One executable serves 2048, HD and Fury. Exact supported executable and asset fingerprints are not established.

setup.instruction: On Windows use the publisher’s wipeout-windows.zip. On Linux x86-64 use the publisher’s AppImage and check its system requirements. Open the upstream player and select your owned game folder containing eboot.bin. Follow the upstream instructions for your disc edition and update data. Only the publisher’s package listing was reviewed.

setup_notes.title: Version and platform notes
setup_notes.instruction: The project reports 110–150 FPS in 2048 on an RTX 4070 Laptop GPU. From v0.2.3, the experimental GOW3_NEO=1 setting displayed a race, with no further testing reported. Unchecked areas include HD Fury and other events, HDR and some audio effects. PSVR is outside the project’s plans.

limitations: Upstream early-development status claims boot/menus/saves and HD/2048 races/results, with 110–150FPS reported in 2048 on RTX 4070 Laptop, not a full collection playthrough. New README reports extra render-resolution patches and experimental PS4 Pro mode GOW3_NEO=1 loading a race with correct picture since v0.2.3; not tested further. All HD/HD Fury/2048 event types are not yet tested, HDR RCAS fix awaits testing and new audio effects may have defects; PSVR is not planned. The upstream Linux x86-64 AppImage is listed in the release; Linux gameplay and CPU compatibility remain unverified. No Portcove runtime or completion qualification was performed.

entries.name: World War II GI (Raze)
entries.summary: Play World War II GI in Raze using your own original PC game files.

setup.title: Use your recognized original game files
setup.instruction: Use your own original PC WWII GI data folder, anchored by WW2GI.GRP. Keep its accompanying files. Platoon Leader is an optional separately owned expansion that depends on the base game; it is not required for this base-game entry. Raze searches installed Steam/GOG copies and configured game-data folders. Reuse a recognized copy; do not duplicate it unnecessarily. If it is not found, add its real location to GameSearch.Directories in raze.ini, or in raze_portable.ini for the Portcove-managed Windows player; do not copy game files into the managed player folder, because Portcove verifies that folder. Elsewhere, you may instead place a copy of its complete data folder beside Raze. Keep your own originals; no original game files are included.

setup.title: Choose Play in the upstream player
setup.instruction: On Windows, choose Install, then Play explicitly. Portcove downloads and verifies the official Windows ZIP, keeps the player folder together, and creates Raze’s portable configuration marker so its configuration, saves, screenshots and demos stay beside the managed player, where Portcove preserves them across updates. Raze may ask which detected game/edition to use, because the same player supports several games. For a fixed entry, Change launch details can use two argument lines: -gamegrp, then the local Windows drive-letter absolute path (for example C:/Games/...) to your WW2GI.GRP archive. Use Raze’s game picker for UNC/network paths; this fixed-entry example does not establish a POSIX/macOS path rule. Keep that archive’s companion files together.

setup.title: Keep upstream update ownership and platform handoffs
setup.instruction: On Windows, Portcove replaces the managed runtime and preserves its declared data. A separate existing Windows copy stays yours: registering it preserves every external file and Portcove does not manage its Update, Backup or Rollback, and the normal-profile settings described below are not imported into a managed install. Elsewhere, you and upstream replace this external player. On macOS, use the official universal Raze.app through the normal OS application flow; do not register its private Contents/MacOS binary. Its normal settings are ~/Library/Preferences/raze.ini saves ~/Documents/raze/Savegames and screenshots ~/Documents/raze/Screenshots. A native Linux build outside Flatpak uses its own profile, usually ~/.config/raze. Preserve that profile and any older ~/.raze directory before launching a replacement.

setup.title: Use Raze from Flathub on Linux
setup.instruction: Install org.zdoom.Raze from Flathub for Linux x64 or ARM64. Make sure ~/.config exists in your home directory. Keep your original files and place a complete working copy of this game's data in its own subfolder under ~/.var/app/org.zdoom.Raze/.config/raze. Open Raze and choose this game if a picker appears. Close Raze and back up its actual configuration, saves and mods before updating through Flatpak.

setup_notes.title: Keep the shared profile this game uses
setup_notes.instruction: A Portcove-managed Windows install keeps raze_portable.ini, Save, Screenshots and Demos beside the managed player and does not share or import the normal-profile locations described next. Windows normally keeps raze.ini in Documents/My Games/raze, saves under the system Saved Games/Raze folder, and screenshots in the system Screenshots/Raze folder; redirected Windows known folders can change those absolute locations. A writable raze_portable.ini outside Program Files uses the player folder with Save and Screenshots instead. Custom -config/-savedir locations remain external. Normal save roots contain game/edition subfolders. A custom -savedir disables that partition, so keep a separate chosen directory for each game. Several entries can share Raze settings. Switching a portable marker redirects paths; it does not move normal-profile saves. Close all copies and back up the actual locations, original data and selected mods before changing versions. First Play in a newer copy may migrate an older configuration; preserve its old location too. Keep a working runtime until its saves work in the replacement.

setup.title: Use this original game and edition
setup.instruction: Use your own complete unmodified original TFTD/TFD data folders. Copy the original subfolders into OpenXcom’s TFTD subdirectory, keeping their hierarchy. setup.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
setup.instruction: Use the official upstream download/setup route or a complete already prepared OpenXcom player, keeping its common data and standard mod resources. No GitHub release package was observed. Choose a build that documents TFTD support; an old UFO-only release is insufficient. Complete original-data and game selection through upstream before saving the player entry. On Windows, register openxcom.exe with its installation folder as working directory, retaining the upstream game selection rather than inventing a fixed argument. setup.title: Add the game and manage your files
setup.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions.

setup.title: Choose the Windows nightly package
setup.instruction: In OpenXcom’s Nightly GitHub workflow, choose a successful upstream run. On Windows x64 download the Windows artifact, then extract the inner win64 ZIP into a dedicated folder. Keep its DLLs and data directories with OpenXcom.exe and open the player from that folder. The same artifact offers a separate win32 ZIP and an upstream installer.

setup.title: Choose the Linux or Mac nightly package
setup.instruction: In the same workflow run, download the matching artifact. On Linux unpack the ZIP and start the AppImage. If the loader reports libjack.so.0 missing, install your distribution’s JACK runtime package. On Mac unpack the outer ZIP and use Mac Archive Utility on the inner Mac ZIP, then open openxcom.app on Intel or Apple Silicon. On Linux x86-64, select the complete official Nightly AppImage and its containing folder. Provide the host JACK and PipeWire libraries required by the package. If FUSE is unavailable, enter --appimage-extract-and-run as a separate first argument. On Intel or Apple Silicon Mac, keep openxcom.app intact and select Contents/MacOS/openxcom with its containing folder. On Linux and Mac, enter -master and xcom2 as separate arguments, after --appimage-extract-and-run when you use it. Confirm the selected original and master game upstream before saving the registration. Use separate writable -user and -cfg folders for each game when you want to keep the profiles apart. Enter each option and its absolute path on separate lines.

setup.title: Prepare this title’s original data
setup.instruction: Copy the data subfolders from your X-COM: Terror from the Deep installation into TFTD inside the OpenXcom data or user folder. In the OpenXcom Mods menu, select the master game for this title.

setup_notes.title: Keep your originals and game data
setup_notes.instruction: Windows normally uses the actual Documents/OpenXcom user/config location; an installation-local user folder and explicit -data/-user/-config choices can change the searched locations. Preserve every actual selected data/user/config folder, including UFO/TFTD resources, mods, savegames and screenshots. Keep the two original games and their campaigns distinct even if they share one player/profile. Back up with OpenXcom closed before changing runtime or mods.

setup_notes.title: Back up the actual OpenXcom profile
setup_notes.instruction: On Linux back up the active user and config folders shown in openxcom.log. The user folder can be ~/.local/share/openxcom or ~/.openxcom. Also keep ~/.config/openxcom or any XDG or command-line overrides. On Mac keep ~/Library/Application Support/OpenXcom or the configured XDG directory. Preserve originals, settings, mods and saves before replacing an upstream nightly.

limitations: Preserve every actual selected data/user/config folder, including UFO/TFTD resources, mods, savegames and screenshots. Keep the two original games and their campaigns distinct even if they share one player/profile. Back up with OpenXcom closed before changing runtime or mods.

setup_notes.instruction: A Portcove-managed Windows install keeps gzdoom_portable.ini, Save, Screenshots and Demos beside the managed player and does not share or import the normal-profile locations described next. GZDoom normally keeps Windows settings in Documents/My Games/GZDoom and saved games in Saved Games/GZDoom. Portable Windows mode uses gzdoom_portable.ini and Save beside the player instead. On Linux, preserve ~/.config/gzdoom, including gzdoom.ini and savegames. On Mac, preserve ~/Library/Preferences/gzdoom.ini and ~/Documents/GZDoom, including Savegames and Screenshots. Keep any IWADs and add-ons you placed in ~/Library/Application Support/GZDoom. Keep your actual data locations, original files and mods when updating the upstream runtime.

entries.name: Zeus: Master of Olympus (eZeus)

setup.instruction: Both Zeus: Master of Olympus and the Poseidon expansion original files are required, including for the base-game identity. Upstream currently supports English and Polish. setup.instruction: Prepare the full eZeus-0.8.2-beta.zip from its base release, then the later eZeus-0.8.2-beta.4.exe patch. The patch EXE alone is not a complete package. setup.title: Prepare a separate upstream Linux build
setup.instruction: Use the tagged source and its submodules, with the documented Qt and SDL2 dependencies. Place the built eZeus player under your complete working eZeus/Bin folder and launch from that folder. Use the matching base preparation and text conversion from upstream. Keep both original games and the actual settings, Save and resource directories backed up before changing the engine.

setup.instruction: Upstream links separate Intel and Apple Silicon 0.8.1-Beta.8 packages from MacThings, which documents macOS 14 or later. Use the matching 0.8.1 base preparation on a separate working copy. Copy the eZeus player and its bundled libs together into the prepared eZeus/Bin folder. Place Zeus_MM.xml and Zeus_Text.xml in the eZeus root above Bin, as described by upstream. Keep the complete original Zeus and Poseidon files, settings and Save directory together. This build has its own resources and profile. Keep the later Windows patch separate.

setup.title: Add the game and manage your files
setup.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Select the game executable and its working folder, and put each launch argument on a separate line. Choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, originals, saves and settings. Removing its registration leaves those external files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Close the game and keep a working copy and every data and profile folder before changing versions. Other platforms need their own setup instructions.

setup_notes.title: Keep your existing game data
setup_notes.instruction: The player normally finds originals two directories above its EXE, or through zeus_path.txt. The eZeus root above Bin owns settings.txt, Save and companion resources such as Textures/Adventures. Preserve the entire working originals and eZeus tree, including any explicit original path, before replacing upstream files. No old-save conversion or base/expansion compatibility is inferred.

setup.instruction: Use an already working native Windows Zuma Portable/CircleShootApp copy prepared upstream with your own Zuma Deluxe data and its matching BASS dependency. setup.instruction: Select the actual completed Zuma.exe, not a bootstrap/build script or the original executable used as a reverse-engineering reference. The selected source contains platform-specific folder discovery and multiple framework storage paths; use the actual prepared build’s effective locations rather than substituting a browser/mobile layout.
